a472.speaker: Mohamud Ma’allin, Chairman of the Somali Disaster Management Agency, together with heads of United Nations agencies led by the Deputy Special Envoy of Somalia to the United Nations and the head of the Office of Humanitarian Affairs
a472.name: Mohamud Ma’allin
a472.title: Chairman of the Somali Disaster Management Agency, together with heads of United Nations agencies led by the Deputy Special Envoy of Somalia to the United Nations and the head of the Office of Humanitarian Affairs
a472.speech: Today jointly announced an assessment of the impact of the El Niño rains at the end of last year, which will be conducted by a team of experts from various sectors and aims to evaluate the extent of the damage caused by the heavy rains and floods that affected more than 1.2 million people in Somalia, especially in the riverine areas, and to identify the priority needs and gaps in the humanitarian response and recovery efforts.

a472.speaker: Participants of the conference (Disaster Management Agency, UN agencies, World Bank, European Union and Ministry of Planning and Investment Development)
a472.name: Participants of the conference (Disaster Management Agency
a472.title: UN agencies, World Bank, European Union and Ministry of Planning and Investment Development)
a472.speech: Discussed that around 75 people will be trained to prepare and present the effects of the El Niño situation, and agreed to coordinate and collaborate on the implementation of the assessment and the training, as well as to mobilize resources and support for the affected communities.

a472.speaker: Somali government
a472.name: Somali government
a472.speech: Declared a national state of emergency in October 2023 after extreme weather exacerbated by El Niño destroyed homes, roads and bridges.

a544.speaker: Berchimans Hatungima, director of the Burundian Office for the Protection of the Environment (OBPE)
a544.name: Berchimans Hatungima
a544.title: director of the Burundian Office for the Protection of the Environment (OBPE)
a544.speech: In his opening address, indicated that mercury is a natural heavy metal that is a significant danger to health and to the environment, adding that mercury vapours, when inhaled, can affect the central nervous system and, depending on exposure levels, impair cognition and in some cases cause death ; "Although certain biomedical equipment, computers, lamps and others may contain mercury, they remain harmless as long as they stay intact. However, when these devices are taken out of service, the mercury they contain can escape into the environment where it vaporises, thus exposing those who are closest to harmful fumes. Inhalation can cause damage to the lungs, the kidneys and the nervous system, while the waste generated can contaminate the immediate area of the spill, as well as the wastewater of a facility. It is released into the environment and is transformed by bacteria into a highly toxic form called methylmercury, which is absorbed by micro-organisms and plants and accumulates in the food chain."

a544.speaker: Berchimans Hatungima, director general of the OBPE
a544.name: Berchimans Hatungima
a544.title: director general of the OBPE
a544.speech: According to him, by signing the Minamata Convention on Mercury on 14 February 2014 and ratifying it on 26 March 2021, with entry into force on 24 June 2021, Burundi committed to protecting human health against anthropogenic emissions and releases of mercury and mercury compounds.

a544.speaker: Alphonse Polisi, presenter and expert at the OBPE
a544.name: Alphonse Polisi
a544.title: presenter and expert at the OBPE
a544.speech: Answering questions, reported that the groups most vulnerable to mercury are women and children; that women are heavily exposed to mercury added to cosmetic products they use to seek a lighter complexion and that users must check these products do not contain mercury; that a woman exposed to or who has consumed mercury transmits it to the foetus when pregnant, which may be born with malformations, and also transmits it through breast milk; that users of pencil batteries, lamps and computers must check the brand and contents; that importers are called upon to limit imports of mercury-containing products; and that preventive precautions must be made compulsory at gold mining sites.

a544.speaker: OBPE experts
a544.name: OBPE experts
a544.speech: Reported that there is a major problem in the management of electronic waste, since electronic objects containing mercury are thrown into bins with other household waste and, when discarded into nature, destroy the environment by contaminating soils and polluting the atmosphere; added that an electronic waste management policy is needed, requiring the construction of infrastructure where such waste can be disposed of.

a567.speaker: Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a567.name: Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a567.speech: Announced on Tuesday 1 April that Russia handed over more than 350 tonnes of sunflower oil to the Nigerien authorities at a ceremony held in Niamey on 26 March ; “This oil was purchased thanks to an additional Russian contribution of two million dollars to the Fund of the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) as part of humanitarian aid to this African state.” ; “Russia will continue to provide the necessary humanitarian aid to the friendly people of the Republic of Niger.”

a567.speaker: Representatives of the Nigerien Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the head of the WFP office (as reported by the Russian foreign ministry)
a567.name: Representatives of the Nigerien Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the head of the WFP office (as reported by the Russian foreign ministry)
a567.speech: “They thanked Russia for its contribution to the WFP’s activities in the country. Russian aid made it possible to cover the needs of the most destitute populations, including refugees, in sunflower oil for a period of three months.”

a714.speaker: Public prosecutor's office (parquet)
a714.name: Public prosecutor's office (parquet)
a714.speech: At the start of the trial, made it known that it was not a question of a favourable majority to retain the case for judgment, the file not being in a state to be judged.

a714.speaker: Defence lawyers (counsel for the accused smugglers)
a714.name: Defence lawyers (counsel for the accused smugglers)
a714.speech: Argued that since the alleged smugglers are citizens and fathers of families, they should be granted provisional release pending judgment, because detention is an exception and liberty a principle; they denounced the fact that those prosecuted for fuel smuggling had had their photos "plastered" on social media, adding that despite their "wanted" status, some, on seeing their picture, quickly contacted lawyers and were given a committal order. ; Said the alleged smugglers deserve provisional release because releasing their clients would meet concerns of fairness (some already benefiting from such release) and respect the fundamental freedoms of persons in detention, and that the accused would not evade justice once provisionally free given their good faith in collaborating with it to establish the truth; for detainees with a medical file, their lawyers pleaded that they also be granted provisional release because their ailments are not being treated in their place of detention. ; Unanimously told the prosecution that while the case may indeed be adjourned, provisional release must be granted to their clients, who have already spent some forty days behind bars, and said the prosecution should have had sufficient evidence to try the case because the investigation began in 2018.

a714.speaker: Counsel for the defendant Karim Dialga
a714.name: Counsel for the defendant Karim Dialga
a714.speech: Stated that his client did not contest the alleged facts, told the truth and helped the investigators honestly; his defence specified that when he was abroad, he showed his readiness to return upon learning of the search launched against him.

a714.speaker: Public prosecutor's office (ministère public)
a714.name: Public prosecutor's office (ministère public)
a714.speech: Said the submissions relating to the request for provisional release were unfounded; indicated that calling the alleged smugglers fathers of families does not take account of the fact that terrorists, for example, are also fathers of families; and declared that if they had not turned themselves in, there were means of bringing them in. ; Said it does not initiate proceedings to put anyone to death, but takes responsibility for ensuring that no one dies in the cells, and gave assurances that it would see to it that detainees' medical examinations are carried out adequately at the place of detention or outside in a health facility. ; Noted that a correlation is established between smuggling and terrorism; maintained that it is not afraid of the procedure because there are "heavy means" for it; warned that it is not the gravedigger of fundamental freedoms; held that the threat to public order is also pertinent because of the negative repercussions of smuggling on the economy and security; and hammered that this is not an abusive approach intended to harm the interests of individuals and common property. ; Held that refusing provisional release to the defendants would solve the problem of their frequent refusal to answer to justice, that it would guarantee their appearance, avoid the possibility of public disorder, prevent those on the run from going further away and prevent society from being "ruined"; the prosecution therefore requested the adjournment of the case to December so as not to encroach on other hearings.

a714.speaker: Ouagadougou High Court (Tribunal de grande instance)
a714.name: Ouagadougou High Court (Tribunal de grande instance)
a714.speech: Finally opted for the date of 16 November 2021, with provisional release for two defendants, namely Abdoul Fataw Sawadogo and Abdoul Razac Sawadogo.

a714.speaker: Me Paul Kéré, lawyer for the defendant Inoussa Kouanda
a714.name: Me Paul Kéré
a714.title: lawyer for the defendant Inoussa Kouanda
a714.speech: "For once, the adjournment is not attributable to the defence lawyers. The adjournment was expressly requested not only by the prosecutor, but also by the civil parties. The court examined the requests for provisional release on a case-by-case basis," he confided. ; Announced that the next hearing would be an opportunity for the defence to ask that the hydrocarbons sector be liberalised as in Mali.

a833.speaker: Denis Maximin Gnonlunfoun, Representative of the Mayor of Cotonou; Aba Bagban Adamou, Representative of the Minister of the Interior and Public Security; Sègnimon Serge Gbaguidi, Representative of the Vice-President of the Republic; and the Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates to Benin
a833.name: Denis Maximin Gnonlunfoun
a833.title: Representative of the Mayor of Cotonou; Aba Bagban Adamou, Representative of the Minister of the Interior and Public Security; Sègnimon Serge Gbaguidi, Representative of the Vice-President of the Republic; and the Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates to Benin
a833.speech: One after another, welcomed this unprecedented initiative, which is drawing crowds.

a833.speaker: Professor Ibrahim Salami, Muslim intellectual
a833.name: Professor Ibrahim Salami
a833.title: Muslim intellectual
a833.speech: Delivered the inaugural lecture of FIRam 2025, captivating the audience with his address on the theme “Solidarity and development: Ramadan as a springboard to promote Islamic values and the Islamic economy and the local economy.”

a858.speaker: Ahmed Shide, Ethiopian Minister of Finance, and Edward Chaiban, UNICEF deputy director for humanitarian action & supply operations
a858.name: Ahmed Shide
a858.title: Ethiopian Minister of Finance, and Edward Chaiban, UNICEF deputy director for humanitarian action & supply operations
a858.speech: Discussed the urgent need for a coordinated response to address the dire situation; the discussion underscored the need for development partners to step up their support and provide timely interventions.

a858.speaker: UNICEF
a858.name: UNICEF
a858.speech: According to UNICEF, over 31.4 million Ethiopians require humanitarian assistance.

a858.speaker: A recent report (UNICEF)
a858.name: A recent report (UNICEF)
a858.speech: Paints a grim picture, highlighting the threats to the health, education, and safety of Ethiopia's 48 million children due to a complex interplay of conflict, insecurity, health emergencies, and climate extremes.

a858.speaker: Edward Chaiban, UNICEF deputy director for humanitarian action & supply operations
a858.name: Edward Chaiban
a858.title: UNICEF deputy director for humanitarian action & supply operations
a858.speech: Outlined their efforts, recalling the delivery of critical supplies like therapeutic food to conflict-affected areas in the Amhara and Oromia regions.

a984.speaker: Partners For the North (PFN)
a984.name: Partners For the North (PFN)
a984.speech: Has recommended the National Planning Commission (NPC) as a pivotal player in implementing mindset change enablers essential for the country’s development.

a984.speaker: Vasco Madhlopa, CEO of Partners For the North (PFN)
a984.name: Vasco Madhlopa
a984.title: CEO of Partners For the North (PFN)
a984.speech: Articulated the organization’s belief that a change in mindset is crucial for fostering an environment conducive to business growth and job creation. “It has been 60 years since we gained independence, yet many aspects of our country remain in disrepair. The issues we face are not merely infrastructural; they stem from our mindsets.” ; Emphasized that a collective shift in thinking is essential for Malawi to transcend its current challenges: “If our minds cannot envision progress, we will remain stagnant. We must stop viewing ourselves as dependents on foreign aid and instead embrace a mindset of innovation and self-sufficiency.”

a984.speaker: Vasco Madhlopa, CEO of PFN
a984.name: Vasco Madhlopa
a984.title: CEO of PFN
a984.speech: Urged all Malawians to actively participate in this mindset change initiative: “We must cultivate a belief in our potential as a nation. If we can change our thinking, we can change our reality.”

a1082.speaker: Health experts at the Integrated Health System Strengthening Project (IHSSP) closure workshop
a1082.name: Health experts at the Integrated Health System Strengthening Project (IHSSP) closure workshop
a1082.speech: Remarked that quality of health care can improve drastically if relevant information is efficiently managed, and that proper management of health data is crucial in improving care.

a1214.speaker: United Arab Emirates official (anonymous)
a1214.name: United Arab Emirates official (anonymous)
a1214.speech: Declared: "As the holy month of Ramadan approaches, a time conducive to mercy and compassion, the United Arab Emirates calls on all parties to honour this sacred period with a humanitarian ceasefire."

a1214.speaker: Senior Sudanese military source (anonymous), speaking to Reuters
a1214.name: Senior Sudanese military source (anonymous)
a1214.title: speaking to Reuters
a1214.speech: Stated: "We do not accept a ceasefire for Ramadan as long as the siege is not lifted in all besieged towns and areas."

a1214.speaker: Sudanese army
a1214.name: Sudanese army
a1214.speech: Considers the UAE a hostile actor in the conflict, accusing it of supplying weapons to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary militia.

a1214.speaker: United Arab Emirates
a1214.name: United Arab Emirates
a1214.speech: Denied any military support to the RSF.

a1214.speaker: United Arab Emirates (government)
a1214.name: United Arab Emirates (government)
a1214.speech: Announced their intention to organise a summit on Friday in Addis Ababa, in collaboration with the African Union, to attract funding for humanitarian aid to Sudan; the UAE said it would announce $200 million in funding.

a1214.speaker: Government of Sudan
a1214.name: Government of Sudan
a1214.speech: Rejected the initiative, describing it as a "crime and an aggression against an African nation seeking to protect its land and its sovereignty."

a1214.speaker: Malik Agar, deputy to Abdel Fattah al-Burhan on Sudan's Sovereign Council
a1214.name: Malik Agar
a1214.title: deputy to Abdel Fattah al-Burhan on Sudan's Sovereign Council
a1214.speech: Stressed the UAE's alleged complicity in the conflict.

a1214.speaker: Emirati representative (anonymous)
a1214.name: Emirati representative (anonymous)
a1214.speech: Declared in response: "Unfortunately, the Sudanese army has sought to distort the role of the United Arab Emirates by falsifying the facts [...]. These allegations will not divert the United Arab Emirates from its main objective, which is to promote stability."

a1345.speaker: Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), Malawi opposition party
a1345.name: Democratic Progressive Party (DPP)
a1345.title: Malawi opposition party
a1345.speech: Has raised alarms about the integrity of the upcoming elections, alleging that the electoral commission, led by Anabel Mtalimanji, has failed to address numerous concerns regarding the electoral process.

a1508.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva, International Monetary Fund (IMF) managing director
a1508.name: Kristalina Georgieva
a1508.title: International Monetary Fund (IMF) managing director
a1508.speech: cautioned small economies, including Malawi, to brace for trade shocks ahead of the IMF-World Bank Spring Meetings in Washington DC. She said the global economic shifts triggered by rising tariffs, volatile markets and declining trust in multilateralism are a test of the resilience of fragile economies such as Malawi's.

a1508.speaker: Trade, Industry and Private Sector Development Partners
a1508.name: Trade
a1508.title: Industry and Private Sector Development Partners
a1508.speech: urged Malawi to embrace effective policies to align private and public sector to achieve a viable socio-economic development. They cited constraints in tourism such as inadequate supporting infrastructure and services as bottlenecks to success.

a1508.speaker: Akinwumi A. Adesina (PhD), President of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a1508.name: Akinwumi A. Adesina (PhD)
a1508.title: President of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a1508.speech: challenged African countries that in the wake of a rapidly changing global landscape, time has come for the continent to wean itself from aid dependency and chart its future through self-reliance, strategic partnerships and exploiting its vast natural resources. His sentiments come against a background of the suspension of the US Agency for International Development (USAid), general donor fatigue and the trade war.

a1508.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs of Malawi
a1508.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a1508.title: Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs of Malawi
a1508.speech: In the K8 trillion 2025/26 National Budget, projected grants at K1.14 trillion with K1.10 trillion coming from international organisations and K86.36 billion from foreign governments.

a1508.speaker: World Bank Group
a1508.name: World Bank Group
a1508.speech: describes trade as a golden key towards ending global poverty because countries that are open to international trade tend to grow faster, become innovative, improve productivity and provide higher income as well as more opportunities.

a1826.speaker: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe, Liberian lawyer, human rights advocate and politician
a1826.name: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe
a1826.title: Liberian lawyer, human rights advocate and politician
a1826.speech: Cautioned the government of Liberia and President Joseph Nyuma Boakai to take cue from the suspension of aid to Liberia and other countries and to institute austerity measures, calling on the President to set the pace for exemplary leadership by cutting unnecessary expenditure: "Recently, with the suspension of aid by President Trump to Liberia and other countries around the world, we find ourselves in a moment of national reflection. As we navigate these challenging times, it is more important than ever for our leaders to set an example of fiscal responsibility and humility. I challenge President Joseph Nyumah Boakai to lead by example during this very challenging moment. I urge him to take concrete steps to reduce government expenditure by adjusting whatever his salary is to a more reasonable amount, say US$3,000 and reducing his convoy to a maximum of five vehicles." ; "Additionally, I believe he should consider residing at the Executive Mansion to reduce the costs associated with traveling to and from work every day. I further suggest a reduction in the number of foreign travels, and that when he must travel, he should carry only a low delegation of no more than five individuals, in addition to his wife and the necessary aides. These are not just symbolic acts; they are practical steps that reflect the leadership principles of humility, selflessness, and the true spirit of service. The government, like any leader, must lead by example, showing the nation that resources are meant to be used wisely for the benefit of all, not just a select few."

a1826.speaker: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe, keynote speaker at the installation of the Bahn High School Student Council Leadership
a1826.name: Cllr. Tiawan Saye Gongloe
a1826.title: keynote speaker at the installation of the Bahn High School Student Council Leadership
a1826.speech: Admonished the Bahn High School Student Council to see leadership as a vehicle to serve: "But let me be clear: leadership is not about title, applause, or personal gain. True leadership is about character—about the power of influence, not over others, but for others. It is about serving with humility, acting with integrity, and inspiring others through your example. Leadership is not about what you can get—it is about what you can give, and what you can contribute to the betterment of those around you." ; said the first hallmark of a great leader is to lead with humility, that a great leader is never too proud to serve and that leadership is "not a crown to wear but a responsibility to carry": "It means being willing to roll up your sleeves and stand side by side with your team. It means showing, by your actions, that no task is beneath you. Humility means acknowledging that, even in a position of power, you are always learning, always growing, and always striving to be better. Your greatness will never come from making others feel small, but from making them feel seen, heard, and valued" ; said great leaders must be grounded in honesty and fairness, must be selfless, informed and good listeners, must have vision and focus, and must be imbued with empathy, kindness and grace: "When you lead with fairness, you build a community where people feel safe, respected, and empowered. Leadership is about lifting others up, even when it requires personal sacrifice. It is about putting the needs of the group ahead of your own. Think of leaders like Nelson Mandela, who spent 27 years in prison for the freedom of his people, or Kwame Nkrumah, who dedicated his life to the development of his nation." ; "Think about the young military leader of Burkina Faso, Ibrahim Traore, who is riding a ten-year-old used vehicle while buying 2024 Toyota Land Cruiser Jeeps for medical doctors in Burkina Faso, buying four hundred tractors for farmers to produce rice and wheat to feed his people, and investing in mobile clinics for his citizens. Think about the leaders of Botswana, whose selfless leadership have made Botswana one of the least corrupt countries in Africa... Leaders like Kwame Nkrumah, Seretse Khama, and Nelson Mandela led their countries not for themselves, but for the people they served." ; "To our incoming student leaders, I say to you, challenges will come and you will face obstacles, but it is your clear vision, your unwavering commitment to that vision, that will carry you forward. Never lose sight of your purpose." ; "Never let arrogance or anger define you. A great leader is patient, composed, and steadfast, especially in the face of adversity." ; urged the Student Council to remember that leadership is "a privilege, not a right": "The power you hold, whether in government or in this student body, is not for your personal benefit. It is a sacred trust... You must always ask yourself: am I leading in the best interest of others? Am I serving with integrity? Am I elevating the people around me?" ; "I want to leave you with this thought from the great Chinese philosopher, Confucius: 'Do unto others as you would have them do unto you.' Lead with the empathy, kindness, and fairness you would want for yourself." ; "Your journey as leaders begins now. It is not just your actions that will define you, but your character. Lead with purpose, with integrity, and with love. Lead by example, and in doing so, inspire others to rise to their full potential" ; "Go forward, not as individuals seeking glory, but as a united force for positive change. Congratulations, and may your journey be filled with wisdom, compassion, and success. Thank you, and may God bless Bahn High School, its students, and the people of this great city."

a1853.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a1853.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a1853.speech: According to the IMF, the loss of momentum is expected to extend into 2026 even if the expected trade war between the US and China does not materialise.

a1853.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a1853.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a1853.speech: To confront the current critical situation, the IMF recommends that states promote among themselves a stable and predictable environment for international trade and facilitate international cooperation.

a1853.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Economic Outlook report
a1853.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a1853.title: World Economic Outlook report
a1853.speech: Also advises that at the internal level of the respective countries there should be an effort to resolve the failures or insufficiencies of public policies and to reduce structural imbalances. The report says that this is essential to guarantee both internal and external stability when the international situation is more challenging, an order is disappearing and it is not foreseeable what will emerge to replace it. It also recommends stimulating growth, when it is perceptible that various factors - demographics, low birth rates and an ageing population, deindustrialisation and technological innovations - may be contributing to low growth and, in time, stagnation of the economy.

a1853.speaker: The New York Times
a1853.name: The New York Times
a1853.speech: Reported in recent days the intentions of Donald Trump's government to close several embassies and consulates in Africa, together with the ending of aid via USAID in various sectors, namely in the provision of medicines.

a1853.speaker: Prime Minister of Singapore
a1853.name: Prime Minister of Singapore
a1853.speech: In Singapore, on 8 April, after characterising the moment in the world as uncertain, unsettling and increasingly unstable, he put forward a set of measures to mitigate the impact of the changes and prepare the island for the emerging economic environment. He continued his speech by appealing for the country to remain "united, to pool its resources, its resilience and its determination in order to continue to be a beacon of stability, purpose and hope".

a1853.speaker: Pope Francis
a1853.name: Pope Francis
a1853.speech: As he said: "Good is too. Let us let ourselves be infected by good and let us spread good!"

a1915.speaker: Millennium Challenge Account – Mozambique (MCA) announcement (seen by Lusa)
a1915.name: Millennium Challenge Account – Mozambique (MCA) announcement (seen by Lusa)
a1915.speech: stating that the MCA plans to publish a 'Specific Tender Announcement' for the project and release the document "at the end of January 2025" ; "The existing bridge over the Licungo River is congested, has exceeded its useful life, and is no longer fit for purpose. It has been damaged by floods twice since its construction in the 1940s, and there are no practical alternatives for heavy trucks to cross the Licungo River when it is damaged by floods."

a1915.speaker: Development Office of Compact II in Mozambique
a1915.name: Development Office of Compact II in Mozambique
a1915.speech: announced that it planned to launch the tender for the same project "during the first part of 2024".

a1915.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) board of directors
a1915.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) board of directors
a1915.speech: announced this financing compact, called the Mozambique Coastal Resilience and Connectivity Compact, the second since 2007, last June.

a1924.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a1924.name: Donald Trump
a1924.title: President of the United States
a1924.speech: Said on Monday 3 February that he wanted to negotiate a "deal" with Ukraine whereby it would offer a "guarantee" on its "rare earths", metals widely used in electronics, in exchange for American aid: "We are looking to reach an agreement with Ukraine whereby they would put up their rare earths and other things as a guarantee in exchange for what we are giving them," the American president said during an exchange with journalists in the Oval Office ; asked whether he wanted Ukraine to give its rare earths to the United States, he replied "Yes... I want assurances on the rare earths."

a1924.speaker: A reporter (unnamed), in the Oval Office
a1924.name: A reporter (unnamed)
a1924.title: in the Oval Office
a1924.speech: asked: "Do you want Ukraine to give its rare earths to the United States?"

a1924.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a1924.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a1924.title: President of Ukraine
a1924.speech: had already proposed last October to reach an understanding with Ukraine's partners on the exploitation of certain strategic metals; in a peace plan unveiled last October he had, without specifically mentioning rare earths, proposed a "special agreement" with his country's partners allowing "joint protection" and "joint exploitation of the strategic resources" of his country, giving as examples "uranium, titanium, lithium, graphite and other high-value strategic resources."

a2143.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) (report)
a2143.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) (report)
a2143.speech: According to OCHA, as of February 2025, an estimated 3.4 million Somalis are already experiencing crisis-level hunger and an additional one million people are projected to fall into food insecurity in the coming months ; OCHA estimates that 1.7 million children will suffer from acute malnutrition this year, with around 460,000 expected to face severe acute malnutrition without urgent intervention.

a2143.speaker: Somali government
a2143.name: Somali government
a2143.speech: In coordination with the UN and other partners, has urgently appealed for continued engagement and pledged enhanced transparency in aid monitoring and delivery.

a2143.speaker: Humanitarian workers
a2143.name: Humanitarian workers
a2143.speech: Emphasize that goodwill alone cannot substitute for lost resources.

a2143.speaker: 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP)
a2143.name: 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP)
a2143.speech: Outlines a roadmap to assist 4.6 million people; it is grossly underfunded, with only 12.4 percent of the targeted $1.42 billion secured.

a2143.speaker: Aid groups
a2143.name: Aid groups
a2143.speech: Warn they will be forced to triage their efforts, focusing solely on the most at-risk populations, without rapid mobilization of resources.

a2143.speaker: Ibrahim Abdullahi Maalim, author (recommendations)
a2143.name: Ibrahim Abdullahi Maalim
a2143.title: author (recommendations)
a2143.speech: Recommended that stakeholders diversify funding sources by seeking support from new international donors, private sector entities and the Somali diaspora; that the government strengthen accountability through robust financial monitoring, independent audits and community-based feedback mechanisms; that international and local NGOs prioritise essential services such as food, safe water and healthcare for vulnerable groups; that development efforts back drought-resilient agriculture, water management, early warning mechanisms and long-term housing; and that donor confidence be restored through diplomatic outreach, especially with the U.S.

a2197.speaker: UK Home Office (letter released by the EFF)
a2197.name: UK Home Office (letter released by the EFF)
a2197.speech: Said Julius Malema had been deemed "non-conducive to the public good" and that it was "undesirable" to grant him entry; cited his vocal support for Hamas, including a speech he made after the 7 October attacks in which he said his own party would arm the group if it came to power; said Malema had made "statements calling for the slaughter of white people or hinted that it could be an acceptable option in the future", also citing this as a reason for rejecting his visa request; said he has no right of appeal and was likely to be denied any future applications.

a2197.speaker: UK Home Office spokesperson
a2197.name: UK Home Office spokesperson
a2197.speech: Told the BBC: "It is our longstanding policy not to comment on individual cases."

a2197.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) party
a2197.name: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) party
a2197.speech: Condemned the decision as "cowardice" and said it would stifle democratic debate; said the UK had distorted Malema's views on how the "genuine frustrations of Africans who are excluded [from the economy] at the behest of a white minority may lead to social violence and resistance" in South Africa; said Malema and the party would not "trade" their "revolutionary beliefs in exchange for a visa" ; "The UK and all of its allies can keep their visas, and we will keep our Africa and a commitment to support the oppressed of the world, especially the Palestinian people."

a2197.speaker: Julius Malema, South African opposition MP and EFF leader
a2197.name: Julius Malema
a2197.title: South African opposition MP and EFF leader
a2197.speech: Said in a speech after the 7 October attacks that his own party would arm Hamas if it came to power; is seen in video singing "Shoot to kill" and "Kill the Boer"; is a fierce critic of what he sees as "Western imperialism", and advocates the nationalisation of white-owned land in South Africa to address the legacy of colonialism and the racist system of apartheid.

a2197.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2197.name: Donald Trump
a2197.title: US President
a2197.speech: Says the lyrics Malema sings in the video incite violence against the ethnic Afrikaner group.

a2197.speaker: South Africa's Supreme Court of Appeal
a2197.name: South Africa's Supreme Court of Appeal
a2197.speech: Ruled that the lyrics do not amount to hate speech and were a "provocative way" of advancing the EFF's political agenda – which was to end "land and economic injustice"; added that a "reasonably well-informed person" would understand that when "protest songs are sung, even by politicians, the words are not meant to be understood literally, nor is the gesture of shooting to be understood as a call to arms or violence".

a2197.speaker: British official in South Africa (unnamed)
a2197.name: British official in South Africa (unnamed)
a2197.speech: Told the BBC it was a "substantive decision", after the UK government had said the first time that he had submitted his application too late.

a2197.speaker: Official statistics
a2197.name: Official statistics
a2197.speech: Show that South Africa's unemployment rate has risen to 33%, with black people being worst-affected.

a2287.speaker: The two presidents of the AJCD and APTDSD associations
a2287.name: The two presidents of the AJCD and APTDSD associations
a2287.speech: Explained the slow process of the project and thanked USAID/KAIZEN for the structural and organisational capacity building of the associations prior to any funding.

a2287.speaker: Said Nouh Gueldon, Vice-President of the Ali Sabieh Regional Council
a2287.name: Said Nouh Gueldon
a2287.title: Vice-President of the Ali Sabieh Regional Council
a2287.speech: Congratulated the two associations while mentioning that collaboration between Civil Society Organisations and the Regional Council is imperative for regional development. He warmly thanked the donor, USAID, and its implementing agency, the Kaizen Company.

a2287.speaker: Hawa Ismael Ali, focal point of the Ali Sabieh Regional Council for Civil Society Organisations
a2287.name: Hawa Ismael Ali
a2287.title: focal point of the Ali Sabieh Regional Council for Civil Society Organisations
a2287.speech: Expressed her delight at the joint launch between AJCD and APTDSD, noting that it is a first for the Ali Sabieh cluster.

a2287.speaker: Representatives of the residential areas of the beneficiary inhabitants
a2287.name: Representatives of the residential areas of the beneficiary inhabitants
a2287.speech: Welcomed these initiatives, which are aimed at improving the living conditions of the population.

a2327.speaker: National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
a2327.name: National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
a2327.speech: Called for the re-introduction of the training of security personnel in Yobe state and the prioritizing of security concerns with physical mid-term/end-year review.

a2327.speaker: Benedict Agu, Project Coordinator
a2327.name: Benedict Agu
a2327.title: Project Coordinator
a2327.speech: Noted at a media briefing in Abuja on Monday that the report was aimed at identifying and strengthening community-based protection mechanisms and effectively addressing human rights and humanitarian concerns of the IDPs/Refugees host communities; said the monitoring teams were able to reach 2,055 individuals as against 5,000 targets for the year while a total of 27,667 out of 60,000 individuals were reached through awareness, and that 80 security personnel were trained on mainstreaming humanitarian and human rights responses in counter insurgency operations; said the commission also undertook virtual inception training for monitors on effective reporting and documentation on human rights protection.

a2327.speaker: Quarterly report of the Project: Protection of Forcibly Displaced Persons through Human Rights Monitoring in the North Eastern States
a2327.name: Quarterly report of the Project: Protection of Forcibly Displaced Persons through Human Rights Monitoring in the North Eastern States
a2327.speech: Suggested the need for improved resources - vehicles, laptops, solar panel and phones - and increased stipend for the Task Team/Human Rights Monitors for effective/efficient service delivery.

a2327.speaker: Tony Ojukwu, Executive Secretary of the National Human Rights Commission
a2327.name: Tony Ojukwu
a2327.title: Executive Secretary of the National Human Rights Commission
a2327.speech: Said the purpose of the project is to enable the government and other humanitarian actors to intervene and respond to the needs and reduce the vulnerability of Forcibly Displaced Persons: "It is with great pleasure that I welcome you all to the occasion of the presentation of the Quarterly Report of the Project: Protection of Forcibly Displaced Persons through Human Rights Monitoring in the North Eastern States in partnership with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). The project focuses on monitoring and reporting the situation of the Forcibly Displaced Persons in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe states." ; "The objective of the project is to monitor the human rights and Protection situation in the project states with the aim of gaining a comprehensive insight into the issues concerning the Forcibly Displaced Persons (IDPs/Returnees etc), to enable the government and other humanitarian actors intervene and respond to their needs, and thus reduce their vulnerability." ; "The Commission and the UNHCR have been in this partnership for the past 9 years. It has become increasingly apparent that the Commission and its partner create a forum to enlighten other stakeholders on its activities in the project states." ; "This presentation will provide stakeholders with an overview and analysis of human rights issues relating to the Forcibly Displaced Persons as observed and documented by the Human Right Monitors in the Project states." ; "The Commission appreciates UNHCR for their continued support since 2015 on this project. The Commission equally looks forward to more collaboration between it and other agencies in furtherance of our common goal of promoting and protecting human rights and giving humanitarian assistance to the Forcibly Displaced Persons in the project states and Nigeria in general."

a2329.speaker: Gervais Ndirakobuca, Prime Minister of Burundi
a2329.name: Gervais Ndirakobuca
a2329.title: Prime Minister of Burundi
a2329.speech: Stated that monitoring the performance of projects financed by the World Bank is a very important activity for the Government of Burundi, that the vision of making Burundi an emerging country by 2040 and developed by 2060 testifies to the government's commitment to the well-being of the population, and that achieving this vision requires combining the efforts of the Government of Burundi and its development partners, the World Bank remaining a reliable partner through its technical and financial support.

a2329.speaker: Gervais Ndirakobuca, Prime Minister of Burundi
a2329.name: Gervais Ndirakobuca
a2329.title: Prime Minister of Burundi
a2329.speech: Specified that thanks to its funding the World Bank has contributed to mitigating social inequalities, improving the living conditions of the most vulnerable populations and strengthening human capital; stressed that there is still a way to go to achieve the development objectives; said Burundi has chosen to deploy its internal resources to support inclusive growth and invited all development partners to take part, and invited all Burundians to be aware that Burundi's development is above all their duty and obligation; recalled that the joint review is an opportunity to evaluate and improve the implementation of these projects.

a2329.speaker: Albert G. Zeufack, World Bank Director of Operations for Burundi, the DRC, Angola and Sao Tome and Principe
a2329.name: Albert G. Zeufack
a2329.title: World Bank Director of Operations for Burundi, the DRC, Angola and Sao Tome and Principe
a2329.speech: Said the review makes it possible to take stock of the progress and the challenges encountered in implementing these projects in order to find solutions; specified that good collaboration between the Government of Burundi and the World Bank has made it possible to overcome a major challenge hampering implementation, and welcomed the facility to import fuel so that projects can be executed on time; stressed that, given the execution rate during this budget year, measures are needed to improve it, adding that with less than three months to the close of the budget year the execution rate is only 13.3% against a forecast of 25%, and that efforts must be stepped up because last year Burundi had a disbursement rate above the World Bank average.

a2329.speaker: Nestor Ntahontuye, Burundian Minister in charge of Finance
a2329.name: Nestor Ntahontuye
a2329.title: Burundian Minister in charge of Finance
a2329.speech: Said that during the meeting they observed that some projects are advancing normally and others are lagging behind, and that they identified the challenges and issued recommendations; specified that among the challenges listed are operational ones, those concerning communication and collaboration between the management units at the finance ministry and those of the World Bank, and technical challenges; stressed that they agreed to organise a retreat to analyse in depth the recommendations issued and the challenges already identified.

a2389.speaker: John Morlu, former Auditor General of Liberia
a2389.name: John Morlu
a2389.title: former Auditor General of Liberia
a2389.speech: “We must live up to expectations, not manage them.” According to him, the UP was obligated to meet the expectations of the Liberian people, and that managing their expectations is not an option but a duty.

a2389.speaker: Amara Konneh, Liberian Senator (social media post)
a2389.name: Amara Konneh
a2389.title: Liberian Senator (social media post)
a2389.speech: In a crude way, without doing the intelligent thing, nakedly dumped his “manage your assertion” campaign on social media.

a2423.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a2423.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a2423.title: President of Malawi
a2423.speech: Called on African Union leaders and states to strive for an "Africa that is funded by Africans"; highlighted the abundance of natural resources at Africa's disposal, including water and precious minerals, which ought to be fully utilized to make the continent the "centre of development" and the hope for the next generation to come: "Africa is endowed with abundant natural resources, including water and precious minerals. These resources should be fully utilized to make Africa the center of development and the hope for the next generation."

a2423.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a2423.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a2423.title: President of Malawi
a2423.speech: Added that mining exploits on the continent should be used to "propel the development of Africa rather than the development of others", rather than relying on external funding, and reinforced Malawi's commitment to attaining these goals in the second ten-year implementation plan of the African Union's Agenda 2063; he emphasized the existence of various regional trade corridors under construction that need to be put to good use in order to cement integration among AU member states and boost trade and development opportunities.

a2423.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a2423.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a2423.title: President of Malawi
a2423.speech: Applauded the government of Zambia, represented by Hakainde Hichilema, for adopting reforms aimed at creating opportunities for the youth and implementing curricular reforms, to equip them with skills that will drive meaningful development on the continent.

a2423.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia
a2423.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a2423.title: President of Zambia
a2423.speech: Was delivering his report on the preparations for "World Skills Day", which will take place in Livingstone, Zambia this year.

a2423.speaker: Abdul Fattah El-Sisi, President of Egypt and Chairperson of the summit
a2423.name: Abdul Fattah El-Sisi
a2423.title: President of Egypt and Chairperson of the summit
a2423.speech: Thanked the member states for entrusting him to head the AUDA-NEPAD committee, and highlighted Egypt's progress in improving infrastructure and creating jobs for the youth.

a2423.speaker: Moussa Faki Mahamat, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a2423.name: Moussa Faki Mahamat
a2423.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a2423.speech: Emphasized the need for peace to be at the core of Africa's development agenda; he also called for an end to foreign aid dependency, echoing President Chakwera's sentiments.

a2423.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a2423.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a2423.title: President of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a2423.speech: Confirmed his commitment to supporting Agenda 2063 and highlighted the bank's investments in infrastructure development projects, including a trade corridor between Malawi, Zambia and Mozambique; the AfDB plans to invest an additional USD 21 billion in infrastructure development projects in Africa.

a2423.speaker: Benedict Orama, President of the African Export-Import (Afrexim) Bank
a2423.name: Benedict Orama
a2423.title: President of the African Export-Import (Afrexim) Bank
a2423.speech: Pledged to increase financial investment on the African continent from USD 21 billion to USD 40 billion by 2026; he noted that the funding has facilitated the implementation of infrastructural development programs that address the fundamental needs of Africans.

a2680.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a2680.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a2680.title: President of South Africa
a2680.speech: Rejected assertions by Donald Trump that South Africa was “confiscating” land, and said he was ready to explain his government’s land reform policy to his US counterpart. “The South African government has not confiscated any land,” Ramaphosa said in a statement ; “The recently-adopted Expropriation Act is not a confiscation instrument” ; It is a “constitutionally-mandated legal process that ensures public access to land in an equitable and just manner, as guided by the constitution” ; “We look forward to engaging with the Trump administration over our land reform policy and issues of bilateral interest” ; “We are certain that out of those engagements, we will share a better and common understanding over these matters.”

a2680.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa (statement on US funding)
a2680.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a2680.title: President of South Africa (statement on US funding)
a2680.speech: Said that with the exception of aid from the PEPFAR anti-HIV/AIDS initiative, which makes up 17% of South Africa’s HIV/AIDS programme, “there is no other significant funding that is provided by the United States in South Africa” ; “The US remains a key strategic political and trade partner for South Africa.”

a2680.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2680.name: Donald Trump
a2680.title: US President
a2680.speech: Claimed that South Africa was “confiscating” land and accused the government of “treating certain classes of people VERY BADLY,” and threatened to cut funding to the country.

a2680.speaker: South African government
a2680.name: South African government
a2680.speech: Says the Bill does not allow authorities to expropriate property arbitrarily, and must first seek to reach agreement with the owner.

a2887.speaker: Tigran Gambaryan, Head of Financial Crime Compliance Unit at Binance
a2887.name: Tigran Gambaryan
a2887.title: Head of Financial Crime Compliance Unit at Binance
a2887.speech: Has alleged that three Nigerian lawmakers demanded a $150 million bribe from him ; tweeting on his X handle @TigranGambaryan on Friday, Gambaryan named two lawmakers involved in a meeting of January 5, 2024, at the National Assembly as Peter Akpanke and Philip Agbese, whom he said were working under the committee of Ginger Obinna Onwusibe, while he could not recall the name of the third lawmaker ; narrating his alleged ordeal in Nigeria on X, Gambaryan said that the lawmakers set up fake cameras and media to make the meeting with his team official but that the cameras were not even plugged in.

a2887.speaker: Tigran Gambaryan, Head of Financial Crime Compliance Unit at Binance
a2887.name: Tigran Gambaryan
a2887.title: Head of Financial Crime Compliance Unit at Binance
a2887.speech: Alleged that the National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu, demanded billions worth of crypto accounts to fund his future political ambitions ; "@NuhuRibadu invited us to the official meeting and worked through Sa'ad Abubakar. Another key figure in this situation was Hamma Adama Belloji. Ogunjobi was just a pawn; they used him too. This was sold as a friendly meeting with the NSA, the head of the SEC and the CBN governor and includes a discussion of the briber that was solicited by the House of Representatives." ; said Ribadu emphasised that he wanted billions in payouts to fund his future political ambition but was "trapped" because any settlement would be perceived as a bribe, adding: "I guess he really wanted his boss' job." ; "Ribadu even hired a U.S. law firm to negotiate my release, but this failed due to their incompetence and greed." ; "Ribadu overstepped his authority and embarrassed Nigeria in front of U.S. National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan. Ribadu acting like... angered the White House and led to diplomatic repercussions - the U.S. limited visas to the Nigerian delegation for UNGA, and (President Joe) Biden refused to meet with Tinubu until my situation was resolved." ; "In the end, Ribadu overestimated his influence. They thought they could secure a quick win, but instead, they created an international incident, exposing his incompetence on a global scale."

a2887.speaker: Tigran Gambaryan, Head of Financial Crime Compliance Unit at Binance
a2887.name: Tigran Gambaryan
a2887.title: Head of Financial Crime Compliance Unit at Binance
a2887.speech: "The $26 billion figure they kept pushing publicly as some mystery money escaping Nigeria is complete BS. This information was provided in response to their request and was simply cumulative trade data for Nigerians on the platform. This money didn't leave Nigeria - it was just people buying and selling crypto. For example, if you trade $100 a hundred times, that's $10,000 in trade volume, but in reality, you only used $100. Again, just another example of them lying to cover up their BS investigation."

a2887.speaker: Tigran Gambaryan, Head of Financial Crime Compliance Unit at Binance
a2887.name: Tigran Gambaryan
a2887.title: Head of Financial Crime Compliance Unit at Binance
a2887.speech: "They lied about Nadeem escaping during mosque prayers. In reality, he returned and escaped afterwards. I don't know exactly how he managed to flee. He emailed me in November, but we haven't discussed the details of his escape. It's possible he paid someone off, but I have no proof. If Belloji had simply checked his passport for a visa, he would have realized that Nadeem did not use that passport to travel to Nigeria." ; "Nadeem did not escape lawful detention - we were being held illegally. Belloji even admitted that he would fabricate evidence to obtain a court order to detain us for 14 days. Once the court order expired, they were unable to get an extension from the judge. At that point, they continued holding us illegally and had no justification for doing so." ; "There was a lot of noise about using Interpol to capture Nadeem. As someone who has been involved in multiple extradition cases, I can confidently say this was a joke. Extradition is a lengthy legal process, and no rational judge in Kenya or wherever would ever approve extradition for someone who escaped illegal detention at the hands of rogue law enforcement - especially when that detention involved holding employees hostage to pressure their employer. All noise."

a2887.speaker: Tigran Gambaryan, Head of Financial Crime Compliance Unit at Binance
a2887.name: Tigran Gambaryan
a2887.title: Head of Financial Crime Compliance Unit at Binance
a2887.speech: "They sent a letter to the U.S. Embassy and the British High Commission, falsely claiming that we were voluntarily participating in strategic talks. This was a blatant lie."

a2887.speaker: Tigran Gambaryan, Head of Financial Crime Compliance Unit at Binance
a2887.name: Tigran Gambaryan
a2887.title: Head of Financial Crime Compliance Unit at Binance
a2887.speech: Stated further that Binance was made a scapegoat for the naira's devaluation, when it was the direct result of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's "monetary policy." According to him, the Nigerian operatives violated international privacy laws on user data on all Nigerians to target opposition members for allegedly "manipulating the price of the naira."

a2887.speaker: The NSA's office and the lawmakers
a2887.name: The NSA's office and the lawmakers

a2887.speaker: Federal Government of Nigeria
a2887.name: Federal Government of Nigeria
a2887.speech: Called on Nigerians to disregard the accusations, saying they are false and outrageous ; the federal government yesterday called on Nigerians to disregard what it called falsehoods being peddled by the Binance executive.

a2887.speaker: Mohammed Idris, Minister of Information and National Orientation (statement)
a2887.name: Mohammed Idris
a2887.title: Minister of Information and National Orientation (statement)
a2887.speech: In a statement issued last night, noted with concern the "outrageous allegations, misinformation, and defamatory statements being disseminated by Tigran Gambaryan". He said while the federal government is hesitant to engage Mr Gambaryan, "given the high-level diplomatic intervention that resolved his case, we are obliged to set the records straight to stop his falsehoods from gaining grounds." ; "The first visit by Mr Gambaryan and his colleagues to Nigeria was discretional on their part and government was not officially involved. However, when the attention of the government was called to an alleged bribery demand during that trip, an investigation was immediately opened into it, though there was no formal complaint by anyone." ; "Mr Gambaryan's second visit to Nigeria was part of a wider probe into the criminal manipulation of the Nigerian currency through peer-to-peer platforms like Binance, but investigators were frustrated by the tactics deployed by Gambaryan and his team." ; "Mr Gambaryan was released by the Nigerian government in October 2024, on humanitarian grounds and following a high-level diplomatic intervention that ended with tangible benefits for Nigeria. The government rejected Binance's offer of a $5 million down payment in exchange for Mr Gambaryan's freedom, in favour of a more beneficial settlement with the American government." ; "we categorically deny the retaliatory claims made by Mr. Gambaryan against Nigerian officials involved in his case, and we urge the public to disregard these false accusations in their entirety." ; "It is essential to note that Mr. Gambaryan's allegations are not only unsubstantiated but also lack credibility, given his apparent motive to discredit and intimidate those who ensured he faced justice." ; "However, we are confident that both the Nigerian and American judicial systems will provide Mr. Gambaryan with a fair opportunity to substantiate his claims in court. Until then, we advise the public to exercise caution and not be swayed by Mr. Gambaryan's unfounded and malicious claims."

a2887.speaker: The lawmakers mentioned (Nigerian House of Representatives)
a2887.name: The lawmakers mentioned (Nigerian House of Representatives)
a2887.speech: Denied demanding bribe from Binance, asking Mr Gambaryan to provide evidence to back his allegations or be ready to face consequences.

a2887.speaker: Philip Agbese, deputy spokesman of the Nigerian House of Representatives
a2887.name: Philip Agbese
a2887.title: deputy spokesman of the Nigerian House of Representatives
a2887.speech: Said he was "outraged" by the "false" allegation as he was not part of any meeting with the Binance team, but had a chance encounter with them when he visited his friend, Akpanke ; "Let it be on record that I am not a member of the Committee on Economic and Financial Crimes. I visited my colleague, Peter Akpanke, in his office, where he was meeting with some visitors about the activity of his committee, with Peter Anekwe, a member of the committee present. We exchanged pleasantries and, in character with my person as an avid pursuer of knowledge, discussed Binance's activities that did not include any demand from anyone." ; "It was during this visit to the office of Peter Akpanke, with Peter Anekwe present, that he told me they were interfacing with the Binance team from abroad over a referral to their committee. What transpired between the two of them and the Binance executive after I left the office is left to them. I never saw those visitors again after that chance meeting and did not afterwards attend any meeting with Binance executives, the EFCC, or the DSS." ; "I am aware that when this issue was first raised, the chairman of the committee went to court and Binance apologised. So, all inquiries should be directed to the committee, not to Philip Agbese." ; "I have never used any cryptocurrency as I do not have a crypto wallet anywhere in the world, so I could not have asked for funds to be credited to a non-existent wallet." ; "Gambaryan and his associate, who escaped from prison, should return to the EFCC and defend themselves. Instead of trying to implicate me, they should focus on addressing the allegations against them" ; Agbese demanded a retraction and an apology from Gambaryan within seven days if he failed to provide evidence or face legal action from his lawyers.

a2887.speaker: Peter Akpanke, member of the House Committee on Financial Crimes
a2887.name: Peter Akpanke
a2887.title: member of the House Committee on Financial Crimes
a2887.speech: Also denied demanding bribe from Binance executives as alleged and challenged Gambaryan to provide evidence ; "Whatever we did with Binance was transparent; it was an open thing. Is it just to allege; how did we demand? This is the question you people should ask them as journalists. Where did we demand it? What for? Did the Nigerian government not charge them to court? If there were such a thing, why did they charge them to court? It is not true. I have not met Binance executives since we had a meeting with him in my office, in which I represented the chairman and everything was open and transparent. There was nothing hidden" ; while maintaining that he had no contact with the firm after submitting his investigation report to the chairman of the committee, Akpanke said the allegation had been made before and there is a pending court case about it and the firm had failed to show up.

a2887.speaker: Ginger Onwusibe, chairman of the House Committee on Financial Crimes
a2887.name: Ginger Onwusibe
a2887.title: chairman of the House Committee on Financial Crimes
a2887.speech: Efforts to get the reaction of the chairman of the Financial Crimes Committee were not successful as he did not respond to calls and WhatsApp messages sent to him.

a2887.speaker: Nuhu Ribadu, National Security Adviser, and Zakari Mijinyawa, spokesman for his office
a2887.name: Nuhu Ribadu
a2887.title: National Security Adviser, and Zakari Mijinyawa, spokesman for his office
a2887.speech: Efforts to speak with the NSA, Ribadu, were not successful. Also, Zakari Mijinyawa, who speaks on behalf of the office, could not be reached.

a2887.speaker: Top government source (anonymous)
a2887.name: Top government source (anonymous)
a2887.speech: Said Gambaryan was being economical with the truth. "He (Gambaryan) contradicted himself because in one place he said Ribadu asked him for bribe to fund his future political ambition, and in another place, he said any money collected by Ribadu will be seen as bribe" ; "Ribadu will not speak because of a diatribe by an individual. The role the NSA played at the peak of the crisis was at the highest diplomatic level." ; "He had discussions with former U.S. National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan and other high profile officials on behalf of the Nigerian government. It is public knowledge that Gambaryan's company defaulted in paying their taxes to the Nigerian government, which is a serious crime." ; "He has betrayed the highest diplomatic intervention. So many things that cannot be disclosed were considered before he was released on humanitarian grounds. So, the truth is that the NSA will not join him (the Binance executive) in washing his (Gambaryan's) dirty linings."

a2887.speaker: R. U. Adagba, EFCC counsel
a2887.name: R. U. Adagba
a2887.title: EFCC counsel
a2887.speech: Informed the court of the decision of the federal government to withdraw the charge against Gambaryan, premising the decision on Gambaryan's deteriorating health and "diplomatic intervention" ; the lawyer equally told the court that the prosecution had taken into consideration some critical diplomatic and international meetings by the federal government, hence, the need to discontinue the charge against Gambaryan.

a2887.speaker: Olujoke Aliu, lawyer to Binance, and Mark Mordi, SAN, Gambaryan's counsel
a2887.name: Olujoke Aliu
a2887.title: lawyer to Binance, and Mark Mordi, SAN, Gambaryan's counsel

a2887.speaker: Mark Mordi, SAN, Gambaryan's counsel
a2887.name: Mark Mordi
a2887.title: SAN, Gambaryan's counsel
a2887.speech: Told the court that since one of the reasons for withdrawal of the case was that Gambaryan was just an employee of Binance, urged the court to make an order for his client's acquittal and not a discharge.

a2887.speaker: Justice Emeka Nwite, Federal High Court in Abuja (ruling)
a2887.name: Justice Emeka Nwite
a2887.title: Federal High Court in Abuja (ruling)
a2887.speech: Gave the order for the release of Gambaryan from the Kuje Correctional Centre ; delivering the ruling, Justice Nwite granted Adagba's application.

a2904.speaker: Hussein Bashe, Minister of Agriculture of Tanzania
a2904.name: Hussein Bashe
a2904.title: Minister of Agriculture of Tanzania
a2904.speech: Said on May 21, 2025, while presenting the Ministry of Agriculture's revenue and expenditure estimates for 2025/2026: “We cannot eliminate poverty if we cannot lift smallholder farmers out of poverty.” ; Bashe was asking Parliament to approve 1.24 trillion shillings as the budget of the ministry, in a country where 65 percent of Tanzanians depend on agriculture for their livelihoods.

a2904.speaker: Ministry of Agriculture of Tanzania (budget presentation)
a2904.name: Ministry of Agriculture of Tanzania (budget presentation)
a2904.speech: The ministry stated that it will establish 1,000 centres to provide subsidised farm machinery services, buy 10,000 tractors and all basic field implements, 10,000 power tillers and harvesting and drying machines; the ministry went on to say it will provide training for operators of agricultural machinery in collaboration with other stakeholders such as VETA colleges, and 500 supervisors and service providers; the ministry said that to achieve this it will establish one national centre with all the basic equipment for clearing and levelling fields, drilling wells and dams, and providing training.

a2904.speaker: National Irrigation Commission of Tanzania (budget request)
a2904.name: National Irrigation Commission of Tanzania (budget request)
a2904.speech: The commission has requested approval of 382,138,408,000 shillings, of which 308,721,961,000 shillings is development funds and 73,416,447,000 shillings is for recurrent expenditure; for this year the funds are planned to implement 768 of the 780 projects begun in 2022/2023, 2023/2024 and 2024/2025, including construction of 60 new schemes irrigating 147,433.46 hectares, rehabilitation of 41 schemes covering 72,175 hectares, and construction of 19 dams and a further 28 dams.

a2904.speaker: Ministry of Agriculture of Tanzania (BBT programme plans)
a2904.name: Ministry of Agriculture of Tanzania (BBT programme plans)
a2904.speech: Through the Building a Better Tomorrow (BBT) programme, the ministry has set aside funds and specific plans to empower youth and women in agriculture: in collaboration with the African Development Bank (AfDB) it has set aside US$35 million for low-interest loans to youth and women; 17 billion shillings has been set aside in a guarantee scheme window which will help provide loans totalling 51 billion shillings at interest not exceeding seven percent; the ministry will identify and acquire 80,000 hectares in various regions for commercial agriculture and will drill 500 irrigation wells irrigating 30,393.39 hectares in 178 councils, benefiting 58,903 farmers.

a2904.speaker: The Chanzo (prior reporting)
a2904.name: The Chanzo (prior reporting)
a2904.speech: The Chanzo reported last year on challenges in the BBT Dodoma project which, the article notes, must be resolved and prevented from occurring in other projects.

a2913.speaker: Alex Major, independent parliamentary candidate for Kasungu South and former MCP legislator
a2913.name: Alex Major
a2913.title: independent parliamentary candidate for Kasungu South and former MCP legislator
a2913.speech: Has said he is awaiting a police report to establish the cause of a fire that destroyed a grader he had hired to level the road from Linga to Mkanda in Mchinji District; explained that he had received reports suggesting that the incident might have been a case of arson but emphasized that he would rely on the findings of the police before drawing conclusions; and stressed that the destruction of the grader was a setback to his efforts to improve road infrastructure in the area.

a2913.speaker: Joseph Kachikho, police spokesperson
a2913.name: Joseph Kachikho
a2913.title: police spokesperson
a2913.speech: Said investigations are underway to determine the circumstances of the fire; said preliminary information points to the grader catching fire while the driver, Moses Kalengo, was refueling the machine; added that the police have not, at this stage, received any formal evidence or reports suggesting foul play; and assured that updates would be provided once investigations were concluded.

a2913.speaker: Residents of Mchinji and surrounding districts
a2913.name: Residents of Mchinji and surrounding districts
a2913.speech: Expressing frustration over stalled projects and poor road networks that continue to hamper transport and economic activity.

a2931.speaker: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) report, “Downward Spiral”
a2931.name: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) report
a2931.title: “Downward Spiral”
a2931.speech: The organisation said the devastating economic impact is tipping many into a hunger, homelessness and education crisis; based on detailed surveys and needs assessments in 14 countries, including a multi-country survey of 1,400 conflict and displacement-affected people in eight countries, it shows that 77 per cent of people surveyed had lost a job or income from work since March; 70 per cent of people had to cut the number of meals for their household since the pandemic broke out; and 73 per cent reported that they were less likely to send their children to school because of economic hardship ; further figures: 71 per cent said they had difficulty paying rent or other basic housing costs; 62 per cent of those who had previously received remittances from family members abroad said they were receiving less than before the pandemic; 68 per cent said they were likely to move elsewhere because of a lack of work or income; 28 per cent reported receiving less assistance from NGOs or governments since the outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic; less than 7 per cent stated that they had received more assistance.

a2931.speaker: Jan Egeland, Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a2931.name: Jan Egeland
a2931.title: Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a2931.speech: “The world’s most vulnerable communities are in a dangerous downward spiral. Already forced from their homes by violence, often with limited rights to work or access to government services, the economic impact of the pandemic is pushing them to catastrophe.”

a2931.speaker: Jan Egeland, Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a2931.name: Jan Egeland
a2931.title: Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a2931.speech: “An urgent scale-up in aid is needed, but humanitarian assistance alone cannot fix this. The rich countries of the G20 and international financial institutions must put displaced and conflict-affected communities at the centre of national and international economic responses to Covid-19. Without urgent action, this crisis will spiral out of control.”

a2931.speaker: Shayista Gul (60), displaced woman living in a settlement for displaced persons outside Kabul, Afghanistan
a2931.name: Shayista Gul (60)
a2931.title: displaced woman living in a settlement for displaced persons outside Kabul, Afghanistan
a2931.speech: Told NRC: “The price of food has doubled. We have to collect scraps to feed our children” ; “If the coronavirus does not kill us, hunger definitely will.”

a2931.speaker: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a2931.name: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a2931.speech: Warned that even a fully funded humanitarian response would not be able to meet the needs that are now emerging.

a3546.speaker: Joakim Reiter, Chief External & Corporate Affairs Officer for Vodafone Group (Vodafone Foundation spokesperson)
a3546.name: Joakim Reiter
a3546.title: Chief External & Corporate Affairs Officer for Vodafone Group (Vodafone Foundation spokesperson)
a3546.speech: Emphasized the importance of addressing the lack of affordable transport for pregnant women in rural areas: “Seventy percent of the world’s maternal deaths occur in sub-Saharan Africa, and we believe this initiative can significantly reduce those numbers in Malawi.”

a3546.speaker: Joakim Reiter, Chief External & Corporate Affairs Officer for Vodafone Group (Vodafone Foundation spokesperson)
a3546.name: Joakim Reiter
a3546.title: Chief External & Corporate Affairs Officer for Vodafone Group (Vodafone Foundation spokesperson)
a3546.speech: “We are thrilled to see such strong support from USAID and other donors, and we are confident that the Government of Malawi will commit to sustaining this lifesaving service.”

a3783.speaker: Environmental Protection Agency of Liberia (press release)
a3783.name: Environmental Protection Agency of Liberia (press release)
a3783.speech: Said the new administration inherited a horde of challenges, and that expectations and morale among employees and stakeholders were very low as the institution was nearly moribund: “First, Dr. Yarkpawolo inherited a completely demotivated workforce whose morale had dropped not only because of low salary earnings, but they were beset with less opportunities for career development,” adding: “To compound the situation, the institution’s bank account was dry, some employees had been fired for the wrong reasons, and while there seemed to be a deepening division among the staff, the buildings which housed their offices were dilapidated” ; said that just a few months into his administration, employees at the EPA now have a lease on life as their institution undergoes sweeping reforms initiated by Dr. Yarkpawolo and his team.

a3783.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo, Executive Director of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of Liberia
a3783.name: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo
a3783.title: Executive Director of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of Liberia
a3783.speech: Speaking at the program marking the official closing of 2024 at EPA Headquarters on December 20, said that when his administration took over they had to build a team of professionals now striving overtime to make the institution among the best in Liberia: “To understand the situation at the EPA, we created two boxes. We labelled one ‘Grievance box’ and the other ‘Innovation box’. The grievance box provides employees with a platform to voice their concerns in a bid to resolve workplace issues while the innovation box helps harness transformative ideas for improving the EPA” ; “What is your mind? What are the things that are bad at the EPA, we asked the employees... we were only interested in the information and not the names of those giving the information” ; “We gathered lots of valuable information from our boxes. If we saw five or more comments on the same subject, we looked into that complaint. Our employees spoke and we listened to them. They complained about an old bus that broke down frequently. They spoke about the misplacement of staff as well as travel opportunities only to a few select staff. They alerted us about some employees that hardly came to work but were taking pay regularly. They complained and in some cases with specific details on instances of corruption that were robbing the EPA and the government of Liberia thousands of dollars.”

a3783.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo, Executive Director of the EPA of Liberia
a3783.name: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo
a3783.title: Executive Director of the EPA of Liberia
a3783.speech: Said the institution investigated the dismissal of officials and acted on recommendations to restore wrongly dismissed staff, and made changes at management level without cutting salaries: “We conducted spot checks to ensure workers were coming to work and leaving on time. We turned the Senior Management Team into a budget committee. Every Monday at 9am, when we have our Senior Management meeting, the comptroller shows the weekly expenditures, income and bank balances to all senior managers. We approved the Internal Auditors work plan giving them unhindered access to all EPA assets. We opened travel opportunities to all staff based on qualifications and nature of work” ; “In fact, the first travel opportunity we had as Executive Director of the EPA was given to the Gender Coordinator, who had not had any travel opportunities for the last 5 years she worked for the EPA. We subjected the procurement process at the EPA to scrutiny based on Liberian laws, policies and regulation, ensuring that all procurement requirements were met.”

a3783.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo, Executive Director of the EPA of Liberia
a3783.name: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo
a3783.title: Executive Director of the EPA of Liberia
a3783.speech: Reported that his administration conducted 1463 compliance inspections in 2024; investigated 198 complaints; received 318 ESIA applications, held 36 ESIA sittings, conducted 6 stakeholders’ consultations and issued 214 Environmental Permits; and instituted 60 compliance notices amounting to halt orders, restoration orders, fines and shutdowns ; said the EPA has developed, validated and had approved 11 policy and regulatory instruments including water quality, soil quality, solid waste management, radiation, wetland, lead in paint and air quality regulations ; “We imposed more than one million dollars fines on companies violating the environmental laws of Liberia,” adding: “Fines imposed are directly paid to central government revenue; developed a work plan and a procurement plan; purchased two new buses for our employees, one vehicle for our deputy and one vehicle for our compliance department and conducted two policy council meetings and two governing board meetings” ; “With funding support from climate financing, we are building coastal defense to prevent West Point from washing away. We are also building coastal defense in Greenville Sinoe County. We are building a meteorological center for Liberia.”

a3783.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo, Executive Director of the EPA of Liberia
a3783.name: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo
a3783.title: Executive Director of the EPA of Liberia
a3783.speech: Said his institution has made tremendous strides in enhancing Liberia’s presence within international forums, and that his administration signed and ratified eight international environmental agreements: “We signed an MoU with Cambridge University to provide 150 scholarships for online learning in climate education that are worth more than 250,000 British Pounds.
