In Cali, Colombia, we participated in COP16 negotiations that led to the adoption of a framework for sustainable wildlife management, the inclusion of indigenous voices as integral to biodiversity governance as well as a global mechanism to ensure fair and equitable sharing of benefits from digital sequence information (DSI) on genetic resources” ; “In Baku, Azerbaijan, the EPA led a team of Liberians... that successfully participated in the negotiations that led to a global promise of 300 billion dollars per year promised to developing countries to enable them to mitigate and adapt to climate change impacts from 2025 to 2035. The EPA under the watchful eyes of our Deputy Director, led a team to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia where 12 billion was promised to address land degradation and drought across 80 vulnerable countries” ; said the Secretariat of the National Climate Change Steering Committee signed a Letter of Agreement with the Coalition of Rainforest Nations (CfRN) to provide technical capacity for Liberia to participate in the global carbon market within 12-24 months, and: “We developed the road map for the operation of the National Climate Change Secretariat; developed TOR to recruit consultants that will develop the carbon policy, which is part of the readiness program; conducted four meetings of the NCCSC successfully.”

a3783.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo, Executive Director of the EPA of Liberia
a3783.name: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo
a3783.title: Executive Director of the EPA of Liberia
a3783.speech: Quoting the renowned philosopher Yogi, reminded Liberians that “If you don’t know where you are going, you might wind up someplace else,” and said: “This is why we have developed the EPA 5 years strategic plan with a cost of 32 million dollars. Our 5-year (2025-2029) aligned with the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development Pillar 5 which addresses Environmental Sustainability with a Strategic Goal to promote responsible management of natural resources, protect biodiversity, and enhance resilience to environmental changes, while fulfilling the country Nationally Determined Contributions and supporting economic growth and improving the quality of life for citizens. We will officially be launching this plan in January 2025” ; “As I speak to you, we have already developed our 2025 work plan based on our strategic plan. This plan cost about 5 million dollars to implement. Although this may seem a relatively huge amount, our collective efforts, over the last 8 months, are a testament that more can be done with adequate funding. The new EPA, we are honored to lead, is an institution built on trust, commitment, respect and teamwork.”

a3783.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo, Executive Director of the EPA of Liberia
a3783.name: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo
a3783.title: Executive Director of the EPA of Liberia
a3783.speech: On constraints, said: “Liberia owed nearly all Multilateral Environmental Agreements. These arrears are causing the country to lose its voting rights at international gatherings and is not good at all. Can you imagine, Honorable Board members, I will be sitting in a meeting representing Liberia and the big dash board will be showing all the countries that have paid their dues including neighboring countries, like Sierra Leone, Guinea, and Ivory Coast and Liberia will have zero payment and I have no big say in the discussion. It is embarrassing to say the least. Even this year, we have to manage to pay over 3,000 Euros to allow Liberia to participate and get some donations worth thousands of dollars from the IAEA. For this reason, we budgeted 150,000.00 to start paying our dues to international conventions in the 2025 budget and we are appealing to the Legislature to approve this amount” ; listed other challenges including limited environmental awareness among the population, limited staff and limited presence of the EPA across the country, limited budgetary support and inadequate logistical support, and interference with EPA work in conducting environmental compliance.

a3783.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo, Executive Director of the EPA of Liberia
a3783.name: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo
a3783.title: Executive Director of the EPA of Liberia
a3783.speech: Especially thanked the country’s international partners, especially UNDP, Conservation International, the Canadian-based Novasphere, the Food and Agriculture Organization, USAID, the European Union and many others: “We reaffirm our commitment to drive transformative climate actions, promote sustainable production and work relentlessly to achieve a clean, safe and healthy environment for this and succeeding generations.”

a3811.speaker: Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) management
a3811.name: Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) management
a3811.speech: says it is working to partner with the World Health Organisation (WHO) to implement its health insurance project for the people of the region.

a3811.speaker: Samuel Ogbuku, Managing Director of the NDDC (in a statement signed by Pius Ughakpoteni, NDDC Director of Corporate Affairs)
a3811.name: Samuel Ogbuku
a3811.title: Managing Director of the NDDC (in a statement signed by Pius Ughakpoteni, NDDC Director of Corporate Affairs)
a3811.speech: was quoted as saying the World Health Organisation has agreed to partner with the Commission on the Health Insurance Project and other programmes that will benefit the people of the Niger Delta region, and disclosed that the Commission recently held a meeting with WHO officials and made a presentation on a Health Insurance Project for the region: “The World Health Organisation is discussing with us our health programmes. They have written to us, saying that they want more meetings to explore collaborations in the execution of our free healthcare programme. They want to add professionalism and credibility to what we are doing. The participation of WHO in our medical outreach programme will ensure that those vaccines that we don’t have access to, are procured through them for the benefit of our people. We are not only looking at what they will bring to us in terms of funding, we are looking at their contacts, reach, and expertise in the medical field.”

a3811.speaker: Samuel Ogbuku, Managing Director of the NDDC
a3811.name: Samuel Ogbuku
a3811.title: Managing Director of the NDDC
a3811.speech: said that the NDDC was also discussing with the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in the areas of youth development and rebuilding public trust to enhance service delivery in the Niger Delta region.

a3811.speaker: Samuel Ogbuku, Managing Director of the NDDC
a3811.name: Samuel Ogbuku
a3811.title: Managing Director of the NDDC
a3811.speech: noted that the NDDC had made significant gains since it embraced the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) as a major policy thrust: “Partnership is one of the major ways to achieve sustainable development in the Niger Delta region and it is important that NDDC, as the driver of development in the region, stays at the forefront of building the right partnerships” ; said that the PPP arrangement went beyond collaborations with International Oil Companies (IOCs) as it extended to other critical sectors such as health, education, and youth development.

a3962.speaker: Max Tonela, Mozambican Minister of Economy and Finance, and Angelo Matusse, Deputy Attorney-General
a3962.name: Max Tonela
a3962.title: Mozambican Minister of Economy and Finance, and Angelo Matusse, Deputy Attorney-General
a3962.speech: At a Maputo press conference on Monday, announced that agreement has been reached, but only on the Proindicus debt ; assured the reporters they would give further information as soon as possible ; did not say how much Mozambique stands to gain from the agreement, but it could be as much as 500 million dollars.

a3962.speaker: Angelo Matusse, Mozambican Deputy Attorney-General
a3962.name: Angelo Matusse
a3962.title: Mozambican Deputy Attorney-General
a3962.speech: Warned that this deal does not affect other cases concerned with the hidden debts; in particular, Privinvest is not a signatory, and so the case pitting the Mozambican government against Privinvest is likely to go ahead in London this week, as scheduled, and VTB's claims against the Mozambican state are also unaffected.

a3962.speaker: Extra-judicial agreement between the Mozambican government, Credit Suisse and the banking syndicate (text of the agreement)
a3962.name: Extra-judicial agreement between the Mozambican government
a3962.title: Credit Suisse and the banking syndicate (text of the agreement)
a3962.speech: The agreement is described as a "global and definitive solution" to the dispute between the signatories over the Proindicus loan, with all the signatories renouncing their claims over Proindicus and its guarantee.

a3962.speaker: Constitutional Council of Mozambique (2019 ruling)
a3962.name: Constitutional Council of Mozambique (2019 ruling)
a3962.speech: In 2019 declared null and void all acts concerning the Ematum loan.

a3979.speaker: Officials at the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a3979.name: Officials at the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a3979.speech: Attribute the findings of entrenched obstacles that have discouraged financial institutions from supporting agriculture to limited loanable funds, high risk levels, and prohibitive financing costs, as well as coordination inefficiencies, cumbersome regulatory requirements, borrowers’ low financial literacy and the absence of robust risk management systems.

a3979.speaker: Official documents (National Agri-Finance Implementation Roadmap, NAFIR)
a3979.name: Official documents (National Agri-Finance Implementation Roadmap
a3979.title: NAFIR)
a3979.speech: According to official documents, the Agri-Finance Centre of Excellence (CoE) will focus on building financial literacy, developing institutional networks, and strengthening risk management systems.

a3979.speaker: Abraham Endrias, CEO of Lersha, a digital agri-platform
a3979.name: Abraham Endrias
a3979.title: CEO of Lersha, a digital agri-platform
a3979.speech: Said robust Know Your Customer (KYC) processes are crucial, and noted that KYC requirements such as Taxpayer Identification Numbers (TIN), national IDs, landholding certificates, and marriage documents often present barriers: “One of the main challenges to financial inclusion is that smallholder farmers are invisible to banks and microfinance institutions. We simplified the process.”

a3979.speaker: Ethiopian Economic Association (EEA) survey
a3979.name: Ethiopian Economic Association (EEA) survey
a3979.speech: Found that agriculture’s share of outstanding credit has averaged 7.8pc over several decades, dropping below five percent of new loans in 2021; identified greater access to fertiliser and credit as key levers for change.

a3979.speaker: Dejene Dadi, General Manager of the Oromia Coffee Farmers Cooperatives Union (OCFCU)
a3979.name: Dejene Dadi
a3979.title: General Manager of the Oromia Coffee Farmers Cooperatives Union (OCFCU)
a3979.speech: Criticised the Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) for suspending loans to rain-fed agriculture in August 2024: “They’ll not lend to rain-fed operations” ; also took aim at the blanket collateral rules enforced by NBE directives.

a3979.speaker: Dejene Dadi, General Manager of the Oromia Coffee Farmers Cooperatives Union (OCFCU)
a3979.name: Dejene Dadi
a3979.title: General Manager of the Oromia Coffee Farmers Cooperatives Union (OCFCU)
a3979.speech: “The macroeconomic reform allows us to retain all our foreign currency, making the sector more attractive”; believes performance-based lending could improve access.

a3979.speaker: Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) executives
a3979.name: Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) executives
a3979.speech: Said their policy shift was necessary to reduce the non-performing loan ratio, which fell to 6.5pc from previous highs caused by bad loans, particularly in the northern part of the country, and that a key issue was the absence of agricultural insurance.

a3979.speaker: Samson Assefa, head of cotton development at the Ministry of Agriculture
a3979.name: Samson Assefa
a3979.title: head of cotton development at the Ministry of Agriculture
a3979.speech: Said some farmers are accessing mechanisation loans with interest rates of 13pc to 18pc, and that while duty-free equipment imports help, collateral remains a stumbling block.

a3979.speaker: Asemamaw Azaga, farmer in Fogera Wereda of Southern Gonder, Amhara Regional State
a3979.name: Asemamaw Azaga
a3979.title: farmer in Fogera Wereda of Southern Gonder, Amhara Regional State
a3979.speech: “It’s sheer struggle farming right now”, he told Fortune, describing paying up to 700 Br daily to hire workers to weed his 10-hectare farm, buying fertiliser in cash and transport costs for a 1,000Kg shipment now totalling 10,000 Br.

a3979.speaker: Melkamu Abreham, representing the Ethiopian Crop Producers & Exporters Sectoral Association
a3979.name: Melkamu Abreham
a3979.title: representing the Ethiopian Crop Producers & Exporters Sectoral Association
a3979.speech: Said his group faces difficulty securing finance for irrigation; criticised the exclusion of rain-fed farming from financing programs and called for long-term finance and collateral reform: “The decision to exclude rain-fed agriculture from finance is misguided.”

a3979.speaker: Muluken Asemamaw, lecturer at Mettu University
a3979.name: Muluken Asemamaw
a3979.title: lecturer at Mettu University
a3979.speech: Said management remains the key challenge, with factors such as land size, terrain, fuel prices, and water access heavily influencing outcomes, and post-harvest losses from poor storage, handling and harvesting practices also affecting productivity: “While mechanisation supports commercial farming, it is not always suitable for every context.”

a3979.speaker: Riadh Naouar, the IFC’s Africa advisory manager
a3979.name: Riadh Naouar
a3979.title: the IFC’s Africa advisory manager
a3979.speech: Identified poor policy design as a key constraint: “Many are copy-pasted”, noting that agriculture receives only three to four percent of lending across Africa; stated the potential of digital finance, arguing that mobile money adoption rates jumped from 17pc to 60pc in some regions: “Similar platforms to Lersha are needed to link financial institutions and commercial farmers.”

a3979.speaker: Tesfakidan Admasu, head of the Agriculture & Development Studies Department at St. Mary University, agroeconomist
a3979.name: Tesfakidan Admasu
a3979.title: head of the Agriculture & Development Studies Department at St. Mary University, agroeconomist
a3979.speech: Stressed the need to de-risk the sector, argued that providing input loans in kind rather than cash would lower default rates, and said a rural credit scorecard could help bridge documentation gaps but progress depends on farmer education: “From weather index insurance to warehouse and food processing insurance, every stage carries risk. The government should prioritise capacity building for farmers.”

a3995.speaker: President Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a3995.name: President Samia Suluhu Hassan
a3995.title: President of Tanzania
a3995.speech: Directed the Prime Minister's Office to work closely with defence and security agencies to accelerate rescue efforts at Nyandolwa Gold Mine in Shinyanga Region, where 25 miners were trapped after a shaft collapse ; also ordered the immediate delivery of humanitarian assistance to victims of the incident ; in a message posted on her social media handles expressed deep sorrow over the tragedy: “I have received with great sadness reports of the disaster at Nyandolwa Mine, where 25 of our fellow citizens were buried by debris” ; “Let us continue praying for the quick recovery of the injured and may the bereaved families find strength and comfort during this difficult time.”

a3995.speaker: Regional authorities, Shinyanga Region
a3995.name: Regional authorities
a3995.title: Shinyanga Region
a3995.speech: Reported that at least four miners had been rescued, though one of them, 27-year-old Emanuel Kija, later died from his injuries.

a3995.speaker: Stephen Kiruswa, Deputy Minister for Minerals
a3995.name: Stephen Kiruswa
a3995.title: Deputy Minister for Minerals
a3995.speech: Confirmed the fatality during a visit to the site on Wednesday ; “We are working around the clock. We have established communication with the victims and they are still alive as of now. I have instructed that all essential first aid supplies, including oxygen machines, be brought to the site immediately” ; has tasked mining experts and the Mining Commission with assessing the site's safety and recommending measures for safer operations.

a3995.speaker: Preliminary investigations
a3995.name: Preliminary investigations
a3995.speech: Indicate that the mining shafts were built too close to one another, requiring frequent repairs to prevent erosion and collapse.

a3995.speaker: Julius Mtatiro, Shinyanga District Commissioner
a3995.name: Julius Mtatiro
a3995.title: Shinyanga District Commissioner
a3995.speech: Explained that communication with the trapped miners was possible thanks to a local safety practice in which workers leave a phone number at the entrance before going underground ; detailed that Shaft No 130 had six workers when the collapse occurred, where four have been rescued, including the late Kija, that Shaft No 20 had eight miners, while the remainder were in Shaft No 103 ; “We are in constant contact with the rescue teams and progress is being made. We urge residents to remain calm as the operations continue in full force.”

a3995.speaker: Fikiri Mnwagi, one of the mine owners
a3995.name: Fikiri Mnwagi
a3995.title: one of the mine owners
a3995.speech: Said the collapse happened while the shafts were undergoing rehabilitation, triggered by underground tremors that destabilised the ground, causing soil to collapse from the base upward.

a4291.speaker: Historical sources
a4291.name: Historical sources
a4291.speech: According to historical sources, there was also the massacre of Jews in Russia and Armenians in what was then the Ottoman Empire.

a4291.speaker: Woodrow Wilson, President of the United States (Fourteen Points speech)
a4291.name: Woodrow Wilson
a4291.title: President of the United States (Fourteen Points speech)
a4291.speech: Introduced his famous Fourteen Points speech, underlining that “mutual guarantees of political independence and territorial integrity to great and small states alike” should be the order of the world.

a4291.speaker: Refugee testimonials
a4291.name: Refugee testimonials
a4291.speech: According to refugee testimonials, atrocities were committed in cities like Adigrat and Axum as well.

a4291.speaker: Ethiopian government
a4291.name: Ethiopian government
a4291.speech: The government says it is catering to the need [of the about 4.5 million people estimated to need humanitarian aid].

a4291.speaker: Humanitarian agencies
a4291.name: Humanitarian agencies
a4291.speech: Humanitarian agencies say that it is not enough.

a4405.speaker: Lagos State Government
a4405.name: Lagos State Government
a4405.speech: Announced that the Trucks e-Call-Up System on the Lekki Free Trade Zone corridor commenced on Monday 16, June 2025 to regulate the process of loading fuel from the Dangote Refinery.

a4405.speaker: Salihu, Dangote Refinery tanker/truck driver
a4405.name: Salihu
a4405.title: Dangote Refinery tanker/truck driver
a4405.speech: Gleefully told Daily Independent that the e-call-Up System is not necessary given the fact that their trucks are not in any way causing any traffic build up on the FTZ highway.

a4405.speaker: Lekki Estates Residents and Stakeholders Association (LERSA), statement jointly signed by president Sulyman Bello and Communications Committee Chairman Yomi Benson
a4405.name: Lekki Estates Residents and Stakeholders Association (LERSA)
a4405.title: statement jointly signed by president Sulyman Bello and Communications Committee Chairman Yomi Benson
a4405.speech: Stated that the initiative which began on Monday, would restore sanity to the corridor ; added that it would regulate the movement of articulated vehicles, avoiding a repeat of the Apapa gridlock.

a4405.speaker: Lekki Estates Residents and Stakeholders Association (LERSA)
a4405.name: Lekki Estates Residents and Stakeholders Association (LERSA)
a4405.speech: Warned against the plot to undermine the reintroduction of an electronic call-up system for tankers and articulated trucks along the Lekki-Epe Expressway area of Lagos State ; “For the avoidance of doubt, we are strongly opposed to any manifest or clandestine attempts to undermine, sabotage or otherwise frustrate this noble initiative, which is designed to keep residents of the Lekki Peninsula safe.”

a4405.speaker: Lekki Estates Residents and Stakeholders Association (LERSA)
a4405.name: Lekki Estates Residents and Stakeholders Association (LERSA)
a4405.speech: Said unregulated trucking activities had made life unbearable for residents of the Lekki Peninsula, with children spending up to seven hours in traffic, routine accidents, environmental pollution, and massive economic losses becoming part of daily life ; “As representatives of residents and stakeholders of the Lekki Peninsula, it has to be emphasised that our children, wards, spouses and neighbours as well as other stakeholders are the ones at the terrible receiving end of the current havoc that unregulated operation of trucks and tankers wreaks... For the records, residents have had to contend with the increased trucking activities with a corresponding upsurge in road accidents, pollution of the environment, unwarranted damage to public infrastructures and incessant traffic gridlock running into several hours with attendant loss of revenue and productivity. Having children in school buses spend three hours in the morning and four hours on the homeward journey has become a reality that perpetually saddens parents and other residents of the Lekki Peninsula.”

a4405.speaker: Lekki Estates Residents and Stakeholders Association (LERSA)
a4405.name: Lekki Estates Residents and Stakeholders Association (LERSA)
a4405.speech: Commended Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu and the Commissioner for Transport, Seun Osiyemi, for the initiative ; also urged all stakeholders, especially those in the logistics and petroleum sectors, to support the rollout.

a4405.speaker: Oluwaseun (Seun) Osiyemi, Lagos State Commissioner for Transportation
a4405.name: Oluwaseun (Seun) Osiyemi
a4405.title: Lagos State Commissioner for Transportation
a4405.speech: Disclosed the development in a statement issued on Sunday by Bolanle Ogunlola, Deputy Director of Public Affairs at the ministry; said the decision followed the growing pressure on the corridor due to increased traffic from articulated trucks linked to major industrial operations in the area, including the Dangote Refinery, the Lekki Deep Sea Port, and other oil and gas facilities ; “The enforcement of the e-call-up system becomes necessary to address the persistent congestion and to ensure a more efficient movement of goods and services in the corridor.” ; noted that although 360 to 400 trucks currently operate daily in the area, projections show that figure could rise to as high as 4,000 trucks daily with full operations at the Dangote Refinery.

a4604.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4604.name: Donald Trump
a4604.title: US President
a4604.speech: Boasted that his government had accomplished more in just over a month than previous administrations had in years; claimed his presidency had sparked a renewed sense of “pride” and “confidence” among Americans; compared himself to George Washington and touted his electoral victory; highlighted several executive actions, including cuts to foreign aid, stricter border policies, and efforts to remove “woke ideology” from schools and the military.

a4604.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4604.name: Donald Trump
a4604.title: US President
a4604.speech: Blamed former President Joe Biden for high inflation and rising consumer prices; promised to deliver immediate financial relief to American families while pushing for tax cuts, including eliminating taxes on tips and overtime pay; pledged aggressive action on tariffs.

a4604.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4604.name: Donald Trump
a4604.title: US President
a4604.speech: On foreign policy, reiterated his interest in acquiring Greenland, promised U.S. control over the Panama Canal, and briefly addressed tensions in the Middle East.

a4604.speaker: Democrats in the chamber (Congress)
a4604.name: Democrats in the chamber (Congress)
a4604.speech: Responded with stony silence, occasionally holding up signs that read “false” and “lies”; Representative Al Green was ejected after interrupting Trump's remarks in protest of proposed cuts to Medicaid.

a4604.speaker: Economists
a4604.name: Economists
a4604.speech: Warnings from economists that his trade policies could drive up costs.

a4604.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President (letter)
a4604.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a4604.title: Ukrainian President (letter)
a4604.speech: Trump read a letter from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, signaling a potential diplomatic shift between the two leaders.

a4604.speaker: BBC
a4604.name: BBC
a4604.speech: Cited as the source of the report.

a4652.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a4652.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a4652.title: President of Ukraine
a4652.speech: “What kind of diplomacy are you talking about, JD (Vance)? What do you mean?” ; “Have you ever been to Ukraine to see our problems? Come once.” ; “That’s a lot of questions. Let’s start from the beginning. First, during a war, everybody has problems, even you. You have a nice ocean (separating you from Europe) and you don’t feel it now, but you will feel it in the future.” ; “I’m not telling you… I’m answering…” ; “I’m not playing cards. I’m very serious, Mr. President. I’m the president of a country at war.” ; “I’m very respectful.” ; “Many times.” ; “You think that if you speak very loudly…” ; “Mr. President, we remain strong. From the very beginning of the war, we have been alone, and we say, I said, thank you.” ; “In three days. That’s what I heard from Putin.” ; “I’ve said it many times.” ; “Of course we want to stop the war. With guarantees.”

a4652.speaker: JD Vance, US Vice President
a4652.name: JD Vance
a4652.title: US Vice President
a4652.speech: “I’m talking about the kind of diplomacy that is going to end the destruction of your country. Mr. President, with respect, I think it’s disrespectful of you to come into the Oval Office and try to litigate this in front of the American media. Right now, you are forcing conscripts to the front lines because you have manpower problems. You should be thanking the president (Trump).” ; “I have seen and read things and I know what is happening: you take people there on a propaganda tour, Mr. President. Do you deny that you have problems mobilizing in your army? And do you think it’s respectful to come to the Oval Office of the United States of America and attack the government that is trying to prevent the destruction of your country?” ; “That’s exactly what you’re doing.” ; “Have you even said thank you?” ; “No, since the beginning of this meeting? Say a few words of thanks to the United States of America and to the president who is trying to save your country.” ; “Just say thank you.”

a4652.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4652.name: Donald Trump
a4652.title: US President
a4652.speech: “You don’t know that. Don’t tell us what we are going to feel. We’re trying to solve a problem. Don’t tell us what we are going to feel.” ; “You’re not in a position to dictate to us what we are going to feel. We’re going to feel very good and very strong.” ; “You’ve put yourself in a very bad position. You don’t have the cards right now. With us, you start to have them.” ; “You’re gambling with the lives of millions of people. You’re gambling with World War III. You’re gambling with World War III. And what you’re doing is very disrespectful to this country, which has supported you far more than many say it should have.” ; “He’s not speaking loudly. Your country is in big trouble. No, no, you’ve talked a lot. Your country is in big trouble. You’re not winning. You have a hell of a good chance of getting out of it, thanks to us.” ; (angrily) “You have not been alone. You have not been alone. We already gave you, through that stupid president (Joe Biden), 350 billion (dollars) of military equipment. And your men are brave, but they had our equipment. If you didn’t have it, this war would have been over in two weeks.” ; “It’s going to be very hard to negotiate like this.” ; “I think it’s good that the American people see what’s happening. I think it’s very important. That’s why I’m letting this go on so long. You have to be grateful. You don’t have the cards. You’re bogged down. Your citizens are dying. Look, you’re running out of soldiers. And then you tell us ‘I don’t want a ceasefire, I don’t want a ceasefire, I want this and that.’ Look, if you can get a ceasefire now, I’m telling you, you take it to stop the bullets and the slaughter of your troops.” ; “You’re saying you don’t want a ceasefire? I want one. Because we get a ceasefire faster than a deal.” ; “He (Putin) wants a deal. I don’t know if you want a deal. I gave you the power to be a strong man, and I don’t think you would be a strong man without the United States. Your people are very brave. But either you make a deal, or we drop you. You’re not showing any gratitude at all. And that’s not a good thing. Well, I think we’ve seen enough. That’s going to be great television.”

a4670.speaker: PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC)
a4670.name: PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC)
a4670.speech: Has warned that uncertainty surrounding donor support poses significant risks to the country's economic stability, noting that the resulting funding gap is increasing pressure on other non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to intervene.

a4670.speaker: Andrew Chibuye, PwC Senior Partner (PwC Zambia 2024 Economic Review and 2025 Outlook Report)
a4670.name: Andrew Chibuye
a4670.title: PwC Senior Partner (PwC Zambia 2024 Economic Review and 2025 Outlook Report)
a4670.speech: Highlighted that the outlook for donor funding remained uncertain, with potential reductions or shifts in contributions from key partners threatening the country's fiscal balance; cited the United States' recent suspension of foreign aid to the country's health sector as a clear example of its vulnerability due to reliance on external assistance: “The effect of this has been reduced access to health services as the suspension led to concerns of availability of medicines and other health commodities.” ; “The cut also increases pressure on other NGOs as organisations like Cecily's Fund have had to step in to fill the void left by the absence of USAID funding, highlighting the reliance on external support for maintaining health and education services.”

a4670.speaker: Andrew Chibuye, PwC Senior Partner
a4670.name: Andrew Chibuye
a4670.title: PwC Senior Partner
a4670.speech: On fiscal policy and taxation: noted that while the UPND-led government initially introduced tax reforms to stimulate economic growth and improve livelihoods, recent tax increases outlined in the 2025 national budget reflect a shift in fiscal strategy; pointed out that the resumption of debt servicing in 2024 had placed additional pressure on the national budget ; “The 2025 budget demonstrates a continued move towards self-reliance, with 80 percent of funding expected to come from domestic sources and only 20 percent from grants and external financing. This shift highlights the government's commitment to reducing external debt” ; warned that new tax measures proposed in the 2025 budget have sparked concern within the private sector: “New proposed tax measures introduced in the 2025 budget include an advance income tax on remittances exceeding US$2,000, an increase in the corporate income tax rate for non-traditional exports, and higher excise duties on betting and non-alcoholic beverages. The private sector has expressed concerns over these tax hikes, warning that they could negatively impact businesses and broader economy.”

a4670.speaker: Private sector / businesses in Zambia
a4670.name: Private sector / businesses in Zambia
a4670.speech: Feared that the tax hikes could have a detrimental effect on the economy and private enterprise.

a5076.speaker: Cicero (quotation)
a5076.name: Cicero (quotation)
a5076.speech: "Pecunia nervus belli (money is the sinew of war)."

a5082.speaker: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)
a5082.name: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)
a5082.speech: Has announced a Balance of Payments (BoP) surplus of $6.83 billion in 2024, a sharp reversal from deficits of $3.34 billion in 2023 and $3.32 billion in 2022, saying this signals that the Federal Government reform efforts are bearing fruit.

a5082.speaker: Hakama Sidi-Ali, Acting Director of Corporate Communications, Central Bank of Nigeria
a5082.name: Hakama Sidi-Ali
a5082.title: Acting Director of Corporate Communications, Central Bank of Nigeria
a5082.speech: Noted that the positive external balance was driven primarily by a stronger current and capital account position, improved financial asset inflows, and more robust data reporting frameworks: "The current and capital account recorded a surplus of $17.22 billion in 2024, underpinned by a goods trade surplus of $13.17 billion. Petroleum imports declined by 23.2 percent to $14.06 billion, while non-oil imports fell by 12.6 percent to $25.74 billion. On the export side, gas exports rose by 48.3 percent to $8.66 billion, and non-oil exports increased by 24.6 percent to $7.46 billion." ; "Remittance inflows remained resilient, with personal remittances rising by 8.9% to $20.93 billion. International Money Transfer Operator (IMTO) inflows surged by 43.5 percent to $4.73 billion, up from $3.30 billion in 2023, reflecting stronger engagement from the Nigerian diaspora. Official development assistance also rose by 6.2 percent to $3.37 billion." ; "Nigeria recorded a net acquisition of financial assets totaling $12.12 billion. Portfolio investment inflows more than doubled, increasing by 106.5 percent to $13.35 billion, while resident foreign currency holdings grew by $5.41 billion, indicating stronger confidence in domestic economic stability. Although foreign direct investment fell by 42.3 percent to $1.08 billion, the overall financial account posted notable gains." ; Stated that net errors and omissions narrowed significantly by 79.5 percent to negative $5.10 billion in 2024, down from $24.90 billion in 2023, reflecting substantial improvements in data availability and capture.

a5082.speaker: Hakama Sidi-Ali, Acting Director of Corporate Communications, Central Bank of Nigeria
a5082.name: Hakama Sidi-Ali
a5082.title: Acting Director of Corporate Communications, Central Bank of Nigeria
a5082.speech: "The 2024 BoP surplus highlights the effectiveness of Nigeria's ongoing reform agenda. The liberalisation and unification of the foreign exchange market, a disciplined monetary policy approach to managing inflation and stabilising the naira, and coordinated fiscal and monetary measures have all contributed to enhanced competitiveness and investor sentiment."

a5082.speaker: CBN Governor
a5082.name: CBN Governor
a5082.speech: Described the surplus as a strong signal that Nigeria's reform efforts are bearing fruit, noting that ongoing measures to unify the exchange rate, stabilise inflation, and restore investor confidence are gradually shifting the external position into a more sustainable trajectory: "The positive turnaround in our external finances is evidence of effective policy implementation and our unwavering commitment to macroeconomic stability. This surplus marks an important step forward for Nigeria's economy, benefiting investors, businesses, and everyday Nigerians alike."

a5113.speaker: Puntland regional government
a5113.name: Puntland regional government
a5113.speech: Has issued an urgent appeal for humanitarian assistance as a worsening water crisis threatens lives and livelihoods across the northeastern Somali state.

a5113.speaker: Ubah Abdirashid Mohamed, Puntland's Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management (April 8 letter to humanitarian partners)
a5113.name: Ubah Abdirashid Mohamed
a5113.title: Puntland's Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management (April 8 letter to humanitarian partners)
a5113.speech: Warned of deteriorating conditions across the regions of Nugal, Mudug, Bari, and Sanaag ; "Time is of the essence to avert further humanitarian catastrophe," the minister said.

a5113.speaker: Field assessments conducted with local authorities
a5113.name: Field assessments conducted with local authorities
a5113.speech: Revealed that water sources such as shallow wells and boreholes have been depleted, leaving communities without access to safe drinking water.

a5113.speaker: Puntland Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management (MoHADM)
a5113.name: Puntland Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management (MoHADM)
a5113.speech: Highlighted that recurring droughts and erratic rainfall have compounded the crisis, with vulnerable populations, particularly pastoralist families, suffering the most, livestock deaths rising and malnutrition levels surging, especially among women and children ; calls on humanitarian agencies to immediately scale up emergency water trucking services, repair and rehabilitate strategic water points, distribute water purification supplies, and implement integrated water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions in hotspot areas.

a5113.speaker: Health officials
a5113.name: Health officials
a5113.speech: Warn that the nutritional status of children is rapidly deteriorating, with a growing number at risk of stunting and other long-term health consequences.

a5113.speaker: Aid agencies
a5113.name: Aid agencies
a5113.speech: Warn that without urgent international support, the current crisis in Puntland could escalate into a wider humanitarian emergency.

a5120.speaker: Virginia E. Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana
a5120.name: Virginia E. Palmer
a5120.title: US Ambassador to Ghana
a5120.speech: Stated that the United States government will maintain all the life-saving programmes under the US Agency for International Development (USAID) - infant and child mortality, maternal health, malaria elimination, HIV/AIDS prevention and interventions, and essential medicines and vaccines; said that although the support for those life-saving programmes would continue, many of them had been reviewed and changed.

a5120.speaker: Trump administration
a5120.name: Trump administration
a5120.speech: Shortly after coming to power, announced the elimination of more than 90 per cent of USAID's foreign aid contracts and $60 billion in overall US assistance around the world, putting numbers on its plans to eliminate the majority of US development and humanitarian help abroad.

a5120.speaker: Virginia E. Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana
a5120.name: Virginia E. Palmer
a5120.title: US Ambassador to Ghana
a5120.speech: Reaffirmed that Ghana's longstanding relationship with America had secured its place as a vital partner: "No matter what the change in language, how we express it, or the change in focus, Ghana is a really important partner of the United States and will continue to be so. The United States is behind Ghana's economic recovery through institutions such as the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), as well as American business interests" ; explained that the United States and Ghana had a deeply rooted relationship founded on historical and cultural ties as well as bilateral trade relations amounting to approximately $3 billion; said Ghana had done better than many in a number of areas, especially "your conflict resolution structures are stronger as a result of hard work, and this has enabled you to move to another phase of partnership with the United States" ; "The US and Ghana have a very warm, close relationship that is founded on four pillars, historical and cultural ties, trade and investment, goods and services - gold coming from here, gas coming from here and we have automobiles and pharmaceuticals coming from the United States, and cooperation in key industries" ; "So, it is something that builds prosperity in all the countries. It is all to say that no matter the changes in language and no matter the change in focus, Ghana remains an important part of the United States, and will continue to be so."

a5120.speaker: Virginia E. Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana
a5120.name: Virginia E. Palmer
a5120.title: US Ambassador to Ghana
a5120.speech: Said the US had not continued with a lot of the economic growth programmes, but had a lot of programmes to spur agricultural growth and would be able to maintain the cash transfer programmes to the people that were affected by the drought in the north ; "But some of the programmes to stimulate more agricultural change, they've had to terminate and I feel sad about that."

a5120.speaker: Virginia E. Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana
a5120.name: Virginia E. Palmer
a5120.title: US Ambassador to Ghana
a5120.speech: Stressed that the US was not leaving a big hole in Ghana's budget because most of the assistance they provided, of about 95 per cent, was to civil society organisations (CSOs) rather than the government.

a5120.speaker: Virginia E. Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana
a5120.name: Virginia E. Palmer
a5120.title: US Ambassador to Ghana
a5120.speech: Downplayed concerns over the future of US-Ghana trade relations following the 10 per cent baseline tax on imports from Ghana; reassured Ghanaians about the resilience of the US-Ghana trade relationship, which currently exceeded $3 billion in bilateral trade and investment, and expressed confidence that Ghana's key exports, such as gold and gas, would remain vital to global trade and would not be significantly affected by US policy shifts.

a5120.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5120.name: Donald Trump
a5120.title: US President
a5120.speech: Speaking from the Rose Garden, defended the tariffs as part of a national economic emergency, arguing that they were necessary to protect domestic manufacturing and counter decades of what he described as "unfair economic practices."

a5136.speaker: Leslie Maasdorp, CEO of British International Investment, and Hans-Peter Lankes, managing director of ODI Global (Project Syndicate commentary)
a5136.name: Leslie Maasdorp
a5136.title: CEO of British International Investment, and Hans-Peter Lankes, managing director of ODI Global (Project Syndicate commentary)
a5136.speech: Write that as development-finance institutions (DFIs) push the envelope, the backing of government shareholders becomes essential for evolving their mandates and operational tools, and that flexibility, control, and long-term vision are crucial; they argue that with rich governments reducing foreign aid budgets, the onus is on DFIs to create opportunities in critical sectors that may otherwise remain overlooked. They argue that DFIs should sponsor new commercial ventures only when they identify an urgent unmet development need and have exhausted other possibilities; that shareholders should change the rules under which DFIs and development banks operate to allow them to establish companies and should develop solutions, similar to the World Bank's Private Sector Window, that increase their risk-bearing capacity; and that moving beyond the traditional demand-led model would increase their potential for impact, especially after many governments made massive cuts to foreign aid.

a5136.speaker: ODI Global (report)
a5136.name: ODI Global (report)
a5136.speech: A new report by ODI Global shows that some DFIs are taking a more proactive approach when a development need is not being met by a suitable business that seeks capital — they are starting commercial ventures of their own; the 12 ventures featured in the report have already achieved significant scale, deploying more than four billion dollars of capital from DFIs and raising three billion dollars from private investors.

a5136.speaker: Observers/critics of blended finance (unnamed)
a5136.name: Observers/critics of blended finance (unnamed)
a5136.speech: Some observers lament that blended finance has not scaled as rapidly as hoped, while others are concerned that it has sacrificed development impact to mobilise private capital.

a5136.speaker: Leaders of DFIs (unnamed)
a5136.name: Leaders of DFIs (unnamed)
a5136.speech: Are often uncomfortable with this idea, arguing that they know how to choose management teams to support, not how to run companies.

a5174.speaker: Experts
a5174.name: Experts
a5174.speech: Suggest alternatives such as microorganism fertilisers, for which there is scant awareness.

a5231.speaker: International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR), Article 11
a5231.name: International Covenant on Economic
a5231.title: Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR), Article 11
a5231.speech: Under Article 11, citizens are entitled to an adequate standard of living, including sufficient food, clothing, and housing.

a5231.speaker: Ethiopian government
a5231.name: Ethiopian government
a5231.speech: announced a staggering increase in public service fees, raising costs by up to 700 per cent for essential services such as electricity, telecommunications, water, and crucial documents like passports and other identification certificates.

a5508.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5508.name: Donald Trump
a5508.title: US President
a5508.speech: Announced his plan to take control of the Gaza Strip and asserted on Thursday that the United States would control the Gaza Strip at the end of the war between Israel and Hamas, once the enclave's Palestinian population had been rehoused outside the territory, which according to him would not require the deployment of American soldiers there.

a5508.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5508.name: Donald Trump
a5508.title: US President
a5508.speech: Threatened to cut aid to Arab countries that refuse to host Palestinians; referring to the Jordanian leader, told journalists on Monday, “I think he will take” refugees; asked about a possible suspension of American aid to the Hashemite kingdom and to Egypt if those two countries refused to take in Palestinians, replied that he might “possibly” take that measure.

a5508.speaker: King Abdullah II of Jordan
a5508.name: King Abdullah II of Jordan
a5508.speech: Rejected Donald Trump's plan to annex any territory and to displace the Palestinians, and is expected to warn the occupant of the White House on Tuesday that such a plan could provoke chaos in the region and threaten Israel's very survival.

a5508.speaker: Hamas
a5508.name: Hamas
a5508.speech: Announced on Monday that it was postponing indefinitely the release of hostages scheduled for Saturday, accusing the Hebrew state of violating the ceasefire agreement in the Palestinian enclave.

a5509.name: The New Nigerian (newspaper front page)
a5509.speech: Reported, “Defectors won't save you from losing in 2027, PDP Tells APC.”

a5509.name: Amebo Newspaper (newspaper front page)
