a5555.speaker: The government of Tanzania
a5555.name: The government of Tanzania
a5555.speech: Has reassured the public that the Fire and Rescue Force is working tirelessly around the clock to rescue all mine workers trapped in the Nyandolwa Gold Mine in Shinyanga.

a5555.speaker: Daniel Sillo, Deputy Minister for Home Affairs
a5555.name: Daniel Sillo
a5555.title: Deputy Minister for Home Affairs
a5555.speech: Visited the site over the weekend and reaffirmed the commitment of rescue teams to continue their efforts without pause ; insisted the critical importance of strict adherence to safety procedures in mining operations and urged mine owners across the country to prioritise safe working conditions to prevent such tragedies.

a5555.speaker: Julius Mtatiro, Shinyanga District Commissioner
a5555.name: Julius Mtatiro
a5555.title: Shinyanga District Commissioner
a5555.speech: Vowed to persist until all missing workers are found and brought to safety: "We must keep fighting until everyone is out safely. President Samia Suluhu Hassan has issued special directives which are being actively implemented, including reinforcements from the Prime Minister's Office and the Fire and Rescue Force." ; "We are in constant contact with rescue teams and progress is being made. We urge residents to remain calm as operations continue at full force."

a5555.speaker: Julius Mtatiro, Shinyanga District Commissioner
a5555.name: Julius Mtatiro
a5555.title: Shinyanga District Commissioner
a5555.speech: Detailed that Shaft No 130 had six workers when the collapse occurred; four were rescued (including the late Kija). Shaft No 20 had eight miners and the remainder were in Shaft No 103.

a5555.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a5555.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
a5555.title: President of Tanzania
a5555.speech: Has instructed the Prime Minister's Office to collaborate closely with defence and security agencies to accelerate rescue operations and ordered immediate humanitarian assistance for the victims ; in a message posted on her social media last Thursday, expressed deep sorrow over the tragedy: "I have received with great sadness reports of the disaster at Nyandolwa Mine, where 25 of our fellow citizens were trapped by debris. Let us continue praying for the quick recovery of the injured and may the bereaved families find strength and comfort during this difficult time."

a5555.speaker: Regional authorities
a5555.name: Regional authorities
a5555.speech: Confirmed that four miners had been rescued, although 27-year-old Emanuel Kija later succumbed to injuries sustained during the incident.

a5555.speaker: Stephen Kiruswa, Deputy Minister for Minerals
a5555.name: Stephen Kiruswa
a5555.title: Deputy Minister for Minerals
a5555.speech: Visited the site on Wednesday and confirmed Kija's death: "We are working around the clock. Communication with the trapped miners has been established and they are still alive as of now. I have instructed that all necessary first aid supplies, including oxygen machines, be brought to the site immediately."

a5555.speaker: Preliminary investigations
a5555.name: Preliminary investigations
a5555.speech: Suggest that the mining shafts were constructed too close to each other, requiring frequent repairs to prevent erosion and collapse.

a5555.speaker: Fikiri Mnwagi, one of the mine owners
a5555.name: Fikiri Mnwagi
a5555.title: one of the mine owners
a5555.speech: Explained that the collapse happened during rehabilitation works on the shafts, triggered by underground tremors that destabilised the ground, causing the soil to collapse from the base upwards.

a5627.speaker: Government of Niger (draft 2025 finance ordinance, approved in the Council of Ministers of 31 December 2024)
a5627.name: Government of Niger (draft 2025 finance ordinance
a5627.title: approved in the Council of Ministers of 31 December 2024)
a5627.speech: The text introduces a series of new tax measures intended to revive the economy and strengthen public revenues, including a tax on capital gains from the transfer of mining titles, a revision of the list of exemptions from the tax on profits (ISB) and an increase in that tax's rate for non-residents, VAT on online sales, a new tax on temporary admissions, a registration requirement for public purchase orders and a minimum stamp duty on tax documents; it exempts the profession of journalist from the taxation regime, exempts new goods and passenger transport vehicles from import duties and taxes, and subjects NGOs, projects and development associations to the duty of disclosure. The bill, drawn up within the framework of the 2025-2027 budget orientations, aims to revive the economy and increase the purchasing power of the population in a context marked by international crises and by the effects of the economic and financial sanctions suffered by the country following the military coup d'état of 26 July 2023.

a5790.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) (press statement sent to the newsroom)
a5790.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) (press statement sent to the newsroom)
a5790.speech: According to a statement sent to our newsroom, the signing of the Financing Agreement between the Governments of Mozambique and the United States, through the MCC, is scheduled for September this year in Washington DC.

a5835.speaker: Chas Everitt International Property Group
a5835.name: Chas Everitt International Property Group
a5835.speech: Says it is looking to expand its footprint into several new countries across the continent.

a5835.speaker: Barry Davies, Chas Everitt COO
a5835.name: Barry Davies
a5835.title: Chas Everitt COO
a5835.speech: Said that despite some challenges, including currency instability and regulatory uncertainties, the group believes that Zimbabwe's residential real estate sector holds tremendous potential for growth: "We are highly cognisant of the fundamental role that the real estate and housing sector plays in driving economic development, and we strongly believe that our entry is more than just a business expansion; it is a vote of confidence in Zimbabwe's future." ; He said Zimbabwe's residential real estate sector is expected to be worth over US$85 billion this year and grow at an annual rate exceeding five percent ; "Our decision to expand into Zimbabwe is a testament to the country's steady economic recovery and its rapid growth in key industries such as mining, tourism, and agriculture." ; "The surge in diaspora spending, coupled with government policy reforms and infrastructure developments, has created a thriving property market that is attracting affluent buyers and investors from around the world." ; He added that the group will cater to the growing demand for prime residential properties in suburbs such as Avondale, Borrowdale, and Mount Pleasant.

a5835.speaker: Vimbai Nyemba, permanent secretary for Legal Affairs of Zimbabwe
a5835.name: Vimbai Nyemba
a5835.title: permanent secretary for Legal Affairs of Zimbabwe
a5835.speech: Said Zimbabwe strives to create an enabling environment that attracts investors: "Our ministry plays an instrumental role in shaping Zimbabwe's economic trajectory by ensuring that our legal frameworks are conducive to investment while also safeguarding national interests." ; She highlighted that legal certainty, contract enforcement and protection of property rights are critical factors in maintaining investor confidence: "We are steadfast in our commitment to strengthening Zimbabwe's legal environment and upholding the rule of law there by creating a stable and predictable business climate." ; Nyemba commended Chas Everitt for establishing its footprint in Zimbabwe, highlighting that it is a clear testament of the confidence that international investors have in the country's resilience, potential and unwavering commitment to economic transformation.

a5844.speaker: UN Secretary-General (message for the 79th anniversary of the United Nations)
a5844.name: UN Secretary-General (message for the 79th anniversary of the United Nations)
a5844.speech: "The UN was created by the world, for the world."

a6168.speaker: Financial experts at the African Development Bank Annual Meetings
a6168.name: Financial experts at the African Development Bank Annual Meetings
a6168.speech: Revealed on Thursday that Africa possesses more than 165 billion dollars of untapped domestic capital that could boost the continent’s development and reduce its dependence on volatile external financing.

a6168.speaker: Abena Amoah, Director General of the Ghana Stock Exchange
a6168.name: Abena Amoah
a6168.title: Director General of the Ghana Stock Exchange
a6168.speech: “In West Africa alone, between Ghana and Nigeria, we have pension funds that represent close to 40 billion dollars and that place more than 90% of their assets under management in government securities, on the pretext that they have no investment opportunities” ; also highlighted a striking paradox: according to her, in 2024 Africans invested 125 billion dollars in cryptocurrencies, with Nigeria alone contributing 65 billion, becoming the world’s second-largest base of crypto investors after India.

a6168.speaker: Denys Denya, Executive Vice-President of Afreximbank
a6168.name: Denys Denya
a6168.title: Executive Vice-President of Afreximbank
a6168.speech: Presented encouraging results with the Central Bank Deposit Programme, which has raised African institutional deposits from 14 million dollars in 2014 to more than 34 billion today.

a6168.speaker: Panellists at the round table
a6168.name: Panellists at the round table
a6168.speech: Identified several major obstacles: macroeconomic instability, interest rates exceeding 20% in some markets, and regulatory bottlenecks that particularly penalise women and young entrepreneurs.

a6168.speaker: Solomon Quaynor, Vice-President of the African Development Bank
a6168.name: Solomon Quaynor
a6168.title: Vice-President of the African Development Bank
a6168.speech: Pointed to a critical issue: “We are talking about 2,100 billion dollars of assets under management coming from African pension funds, insurance companies and sovereign wealth funds. But more than 80% of that sum is locked up in public treasuries.”

a6168.speaker: S&P Global (rating agency)
a6168.name: S&P Global (rating agency)
a6168.speech: According to S&P Global, Africa should reach growth of 4.8% in 2025, well above the global average of 3%; the rating agency made 11 positive adjustments to African sovereign ratings in the previous year.

a6168.speaker: The round table (“Making the most of Africa’s capital”)
a6168.name: The round table (“Making the most of Africa’s capital”)
a6168.speech: Called for a paradigm shift: abandoning excessive dependence on foreign aid in favour of bold investment strategies led by African countries themselves, with the urgent development of sophisticated capital markets to channel these resources towards productive investments.

a6239.speaker: Joint communiqué No. 024012/MICA/MEF of 18 September 2024 of the ministries in charge of Trade and the Economy
a6239.name: Joint communiqué No. 024012/MICA/MEF of 18 September 2024 of the ministries in charge of Trade and the Economy
a6239.speech: Ordered the temporary suspension of the export of shea almonds, the basis on which the seizures were carried out.

a6239.speaker: Adama Ilboudo, Divisional Inspector of Customs, Director General of Customs
a6239.name: Adama Ilboudo
a6239.title: Divisional Inspector of Customs, Director General of Customs
a6239.speech: While congratulating and encouraging the officers of the customs offices concerned, reminds all exporters of shea almonds and nuts that the purpose of this suspension is to make these raw materials available to national industrial processing units, which allows alignment with the Government's drive to support the development of national industries ; calls on all exporters of shea almonds and nuts to comply with the aforementioned joint communiqué on the suspension and counts on the vigilance of honest citizens in order to prevent such fraud.

a6376.speaker: Joyce Bawah Mogtari, Presidential Advisor and Special Aid to the President
a6376.name: Joyce Bawah Mogtari
a6376.title: Presidential Advisor and Special Aid to the President
a6376.speech: Stressed the need to prioritise quality control, integrated trade, and environmental protection in order to harness the full benefits of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and achieve sustainable economic growth; said while the country had made great strides in stabilising the economy and strengthening diplomatic relations, those gains risked being undermined if the country did not address structural inefficiencies in its supply chain and trade systems.

a6376.speaker: Joyce Bawah Mogtari, Presidential Advisor and Special Aid to the President
a6376.name: Joyce Bawah Mogtari
a6376.title: Presidential Advisor and Special Aid to the President
a6376.speech: Called for collective action to preserve water bodies, soil and the ecosystem, emphasising that environmental pollution undermined every effort the country made to build sustainable trade networks. "Environmental degradation, particularly from illegal mining activities, is a major threat to the country's agricultural exports and overall health of the economy" ; "Our farms are producing crops, but the produce is often contaminated by pollutants, making them unfit for human consumption. That defeats the entire purpose of building an integrated supply chain" ; commended the introduction of carbon credits, saying they provided an incentive to reforest degraded areas and promote alternative livelihoods to illegal mining.

a6376.speaker: Hannah Boohemaa Otu, Group Head Supply Chain of Jospong Group of Companies
a6376.name: Hannah Boohemaa Otu
a6376.title: Group Head Supply Chain of Jospong Group of Companies
a6376.speech: Urged African businesses to strengthen local markets and ensure that locally produced goods and services remained competitive despite tariffs and external pressures; referencing the recent 10 per cent tariff imposed by the United States on African exports, she said African countries must reduce dependency on foreign aid and take control of their economic destiny. "We can create a thriving business environment, strengthen local economies, and support currency stabilisation by prioritising quality, innovation and efficiency."

a6376.speaker: Hannah Boohemaa Otu, Group Head Supply Chain of Jospong Group of Companies
a6376.name: Hannah Boohemaa Otu
a6376.title: Group Head Supply Chain of Jospong Group of Companies
a6376.speech: Called for enhanced free cash flow generation among businesses, stressing that integrated supply chain minded professionals must leverage technology for seamless data sharing, transparency and traceability.

a6376.speaker: Richard Obeng Okrah, President of the Chartered Institute of Supply Chain Management-Ghana (CISCM)
a6376.name: Richard Obeng Okrah
a6376.title: President of the Chartered Institute of Supply Chain Management-Ghana (CISCM)
a6376.speech: Revealed that the institute was pursuing the enactment of a legislative instrument that would bring together all professional bodies involved in various components of the supply chain into an apex council; announced that the institute's special initiative for the year would focus on five critical sectors of the economy - security, health, agriculture, extractive industry, energy - to ensure value addition and supply chain excellence.

a6461.speaker: Emmanuella Zamba, Permanent Secretary of the Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA)
a6461.name: Emmanuella Zamba
a6461.title: Permanent Secretary of the Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA)
a6461.speech: Emphasised the significance of collaboration in achieving UHC: “Your innovative approaches, dedication, and tireless advocacy are the backbone of our achievements.” “Today, we celebrate not just the milestones but the extraordinary individuals and organisations that made them possible.” ; “Through ILERA EKO, we are bridging gaps in healthcare access for all Lagosians” ; highlighted the scheme’s milestones, including over one million enrollees and the establishment of the Eko Social Health Alliance (EKOSHA) for vulnerable populations.

a6461.speaker: Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA)
a6461.name: Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA)
a6461.speech: Revealed that over 1.3 million residents have been enrolled in the Ilera-Eko insurance scheme, noting that since the enactment of the Lagos State Health Scheme Law in 2015, the state has significantly advanced toward its UHC goals.

a6461.speaker: Abimbola Mabogunje, Permanent Secretary, Health District VI, Lagos State
a6461.name: Abimbola Mabogunje
a6461.title: Permanent Secretary, Health District VI, Lagos State
a6461.speech: Commended LASHMA for the event, which she noted underscores the importance of health insurance in achieving UHC: “Access to affordable healthcare should not lead to out-of-pocket financial strain. Health insurance bridges this gap, and ILERA EKO is a testament to that” ; commended LASHMA for its proactive efforts in reducing out-of-pocket expenses through health insurance ; “Primary healthcare is pivotal, and LASHMA is setting the pace for universal health access in Lagos.”

a6461.speaker: Chidumga Ohazurike, Senior Health Specialist with USAID-LHSS
a6461.name: Chidumga Ohazurike
a6461.title: Senior Health Specialist with USAID-LHSS
a6461.speech: Applauded LASHMA’s progress and recognised the vital role of healthcare providers, stating: “We’ve witnessed LASHMA grow significantly, with impactful results that inspire confidence in the future of health insurance in Lagos.”

a6678.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a6678.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a6678.title: President of Malawi
a6678.speech: Expressed his appreciation to local organizations and development partners for their unwavering support and dedication in ensuring food availability to Malawians during this period of food security crisis ; recognised significant contributions that Malawi has received from various development partners through the World Food Programme (WFP) ; specifically commended partners such as Good Neighbors Malawi, Nkhoma Synod, Emerging Donor March Fund, Save the Children, United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF), BHA, FAO, Mary's Meals, USAID, JBJ Foundation, ISRAID, and Caritas partners for their steadfast support ; urged the partners to continue their efforts in mobilising support for Malawi from across the globe to alleviate the lives of Malawians.

a6678.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a6678.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a6678.title: President of Malawi
a6678.speech: Stressed the importance of seeking international support to address the humanitarian crisis the country is currently grappling with.

a6678.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a6678.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a6678.title: President of Malawi
a6678.speech: Said WFP will publicly disclose the details of how and where the aid has been distributed.

a6678.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a6678.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a6678.title: President of Malawi
a6678.speech: Pointed out that Malawi has received substantial financial support from governments around the world through the World Food Program (WFP), including 11.8 million dollars from Sweden and the Netherlands, 7 million dollars from the United States, 3.8 million dollars from the United Kingdom, 1.9 million dollars from Japan, 1.6 million dollars from France, 1.5 million dollars from South Korea, and 1.07 million dollars from Germany; additionally, Norway and Iceland contributed 950,000 dollars, Denmark provided 750,000 dollars, Ireland donated 556,000 dollars, Switzerland contributed 500,000 dollars, and the African Development Bank donated 1 million dollars.

a6781.speaker: Congress of Peru
a6781.name: Congress of Peru
a6781.speech: Removed President Dina Boluarte, 63, from office on the night of Thursday 9 to Friday 10 October 2025 for permanent moral incapacity to exercise her functions; the main charge against the former president and her government was "their inability to resolve the security crisis", and Boluarte and her team were held "responsible for the insecurity besetting the country, which has cost the lives of more than 5,000 people in three years".

a6781.speaker: El Comercio, Peruvian daily newspaper (cited by Courrier international)
a6781.name: El Comercio
a6781.title: Peruvian daily newspaper (cited by Courrier international)
a6781.speech: "Dina Boluarte leaves behind a country that is less safe, more fragmented and more distrustful of its institutions" ; "This is the epilogue of an administration that, from its very beginnings, was characterised by an absence of direction and an inability to confront the country's most urgent challenges."

a6781.speaker: José Jéri, 38, President of the Peruvian Parliament, sworn in as head of state
a6781.name: José Jéri
a6781.title: 38, President of the Peruvian Parliament, sworn in as head of state
a6781.speech: "I assume the presidency of the Republic with humility, by constitutional succession, in order to establish and lead a transitional government." He will lead the country until 26 July 2026, with the heavy task of organising general elections next April.

a6781.speaker: Peruvian public prosecutor's office (ministère public)
a6781.name: Peruvian public prosecutor's office (ministère public)
a6781.speech: Asked the courts to bar Boluarte from leaving the country for 18 to 36 months in order to finalise the investigations against her for "offences of money laundering to the detriment of the State" and "corruption and abuse of power", stating that "this measure aims to guarantee Boluarte's presence during the criminal proceedings and [to guard against] a possible flight from the national territory".

a6868.speaker: Demis Chanyalew (PhD), agricultural economy researcher and author of the article
a6868.name: Demis Chanyalew (PhD)
a6868.title: agricultural economy researcher and author of the article
a6868.speech: Argues that even today, if Ethiopia finds committed citizens, a government and leadership institutions that formulate and implement a national policy, strategy, programme and implementation framework (POSPEI), she can have her own national imperial capitalists ; emphasises that through the instrumentality of Ethiopian economic and political collaborators, foreign forces have implemented their conspiracy of stunting and destroying Ethiopian national investors and capitalists, and continue to do so today ; states that he has made this conclusion known repeatedly in his recent books and newspaper columns.

a6868.speaker: Demis Chanyalew (PhD), agricultural economy researcher and author of the article
a6868.name: Demis Chanyalew (PhD)
a6868.title: agricultural economy researcher and author of the article
a6868.speech: Presented his professional position, in a two-part article in the Reporter newspaper of 2 and 9 Tahsas 2015 E.C. titled “The Narrative that Opposes Cluster Farming”, that the cluster farming movement and project supported by foreign forces' dollars has become an obstacle preventing the Ethiopian farmer from establishing modern, commercially oriented farms on his own initiative and preventing national imperial capitalists in the sector from being born, growing and multiplying; explained that this does not mean the recent cluster farming movement was unnecessary or ineffective; said cluster farming may be an option for raising productivity of selected crops and animal products in the short term, but for long-term structural change and citizen-led industrial agriculture it is an obstructive and indeed fatal strategy.

a6868.speaker: Demis Chanyalew (PhD), agricultural economy researcher and author of the article
a6868.name: Demis Chanyalew (PhD)
a6868.title: agricultural economy researcher and author of the article
a6868.speech: Holds the position that neither the EPRDF government nor today's Prosperity government has been seen to formulate a POSPEI so that Ethiopia would create capitalist imperialists of her own, and that the country appears to be being driven into a command-economy and developmental-state system and opened up as a victim of the corporatocracy created by the World Bank, the IMF and cross-border companies ; says that in his estimation the works done under the Prosperity Party government's senior leadership over the past five years, though many and effective, are very small relative to Ethiopia's present capacity, and that the process of formulating and implementing an appropriate national POSPEI is thin and not aligned with protecting the interests of the country and the people.

a6868.speaker: Demis Chanyalew (PhD), agricultural economy researcher and author of the article
a6868.name: Demis Chanyalew (PhD)
a6868.title: agricultural economy researcher and author of the article
a6868.speech: Recommends that Ethiopia's POSPEI framework focus on three themes: an economy not based on race and ethnicity; creating, growing, strengthening and multiplying national imperial capitalists; and organising a strong army and building defence, security and intelligence institutions ; recommends that land policy change from its present government-focused content to a private-ownership-focused policy, while land ownership must in no way be given to foreign nationals until the country has the institutions to administer and protect it ; recommends citizen-led natural resource development POSPEI; fiscal, macroeconomic and trade POSPEIs based on competitive rather than comparative advantage; free movement and organisation of inputs; and developmental public administration and politics freed from the poverty mindset ; says that Americans deploy their army in any part of the world not to establish democracy but to seize sources of raw materials and obtain markets.

a6868.speaker: Demis Chanyalew (PhD), agricultural economy researcher and author of the article
a6868.name: Demis Chanyalew (PhD)
a6868.title: agricultural economy researcher and author of the article
a6868.speech: States that in a review study paper he wrote in 2000 E.C. in the EPRDF era and presented at a professional forum meeting, he began to argue that Ethiopia's POSPEI formulation must change from poverty-focused to pragmatic prosperity-focused; recommends readers read the English edition published in the post-conference book of the tenth annual conference of the Ethiopian Agricultural Economics Professional Association ; recommends readers read his 2012 E.C. book “The Economy, the Three Politicians and Policy”, in which he and professional colleagues presented a recommendation for revising land POSPEI around 32 major issues.

a6868.speaker: Dejazmach Wolde Semayat Gebre Wold, in his 2012 E.C. book “My Life: The Thirst for Work I Had for My Country Ethiopia and for My Fellow Ethiopians”
a6868.name: Dejazmach Wolde Semayat Gebre Wold
a6868.title: in his 2012 E.C. book “My Life: The Thirst for Work I Had for My Country Ethiopia and for My Fellow Ethiopians”
a6868.speech: Chapters 8 to 11 write extensively and deeply the full history of the movement begun in the Emperor's time to create national imperialists and the infrastructure construction serving it, up to and including the design of today's Renaissance Dam project; from the book the author understood that Western colonisers, observing the organisation of Ethiopians' economic growth under Ethiopian leadership, resolved once again to weaken the country, including by using the Somali government to break it up through the eastern part of the country and by conspiring to divide Ethiopia by race, ethnicity, language and religion.

a6868.speaker: Atnafu and Mesfin (PhD), article in The Habesha magazine, December 2021, “Prochazka's Death Throes at the State Department, Ethiopia and the USA”
a6868.name: Atnafu and Mesfin (PhD)
a6868.title: article in The Habesha magazine, December 2021, “Prochazka's Death Throes at the State Department, Ethiopia and the USA”
a6868.speech: Drawing on Roman Prochazka's 1935 English book “Abyssinia, the Powder Barrel”, presented an analysis of the contemporary content of these machinations and made clear how hard the American-led developed Western governments work to break up Ethiopia, and how they have planned and are implementing ethnicity- and religion-targeted weakening and, where possible, destruction, in order to secure their interests in Africa and in the lands of black people.

a6868.speaker: Bekele Tsegaye, in his 2015 E.C. book “The Road to Success”
a6868.name: Bekele Tsegaye
a6868.title: in his 2015 E.C. book “The Road to Success”
a6868.speech: documents that his father, Ato Tsegaye Gashe of the Bekoji area, owner of today's Becas Chemicals Company, travelled from Chacha in Shewa to Lemu and Bilbilo district in Arsi, became a successful trader, bought up to fifty hectares of land and a tractor, and was derailed by the revolution just as he was about to start modern farming.

a6868.speaker: Andrzej Bartnicki and Joanna Mantel-Niecko, “History of Ethiopia, from the Beginning to the Present Era” (translated by Alemayehu Abebe, 2006 E.C.)
a6868.name: Andrzej Bartnicki and Joanna Mantel-Niecko
a6868.title: “History of Ethiopia, from the Beginning to the Present Era” (translated by Alemayehu Abebe, 2006 E.C.)
a6868.speech: documents the disintegration of the state that threatened Ethiopia in the 16th century through foreign forces, particularly the Portuguese Jesuits, on religious pretexts, and thirty years of continuous civil conflict and war; records on page 337 that in Menelik's time the Italian Baratieri sincerely believed he would “divide Ethiopia”; explains on page 406 that Britain, France and Italy plotted at the beginning of 1890 E.C. to carve up Ethiopia; writes on page 447 that these forces did subversive work focused on organising war from outside and on a coup strategy from inside, including the coup in which Negadras Gebre Hiwot Baykedagn and others participated; writes on pages 535 to 557 that the Italians divided Ethiopia into six governorates, split it by religion and clan and prepared a settlement territory; and shares that when Ethiopians made the Italians leave in 1941 they blew up with mines the roads and bridges that had been built.

a6868.speaker: Emperor Fasil
a6868.name: Emperor Fasil
a6868.speech: ordered at the time that foreign nationals be swept out of the country, having understood these forces' evil mission and country-destroying activity.

a6868.speaker: Prosperity government's 2013 to 2022 E.C. development plan document (Part Three)
a6868.name: Prosperity government's 2013 to 2022 E.C. development plan document (Part Three)
a6868.speech: states that cluster organisation is the main direction of focus in the manufacturing industry and service sector.

a6868.speaker: Reporter newspaper (editor's note)
a6868.name: Reporter newspaper (editor's note)
a6868.speech: “From the editor: the writer is an agricultural economy researcher and professional; while we state that the article reflects only his views, he can be reached at his email address.”

a6919.speaker: West African Examinations Council (WAEC) WASSCE results data
a6919.name: West African Examinations Council (WAEC) WASSCE results data
a6919.speech: Show that the figure of 822 refers to candidates who passed at least five subjects, including English and Mathematics, with credit, while the number who passed five subjects, including English and Mathematics, with any grade is much higher at 28,576.

a6958.speaker: Mawuli Komla Afasi, Executive Director of the project (Engage Now Africa)
a6958.name: Mawuli Komla Afasi
a6958.title: Executive Director of the project (Engage Now Africa)
a6958.speech: Believes consistent education across the country will be effective in combating modern slavery and human trafficking ; called on all stakeholders especially officers from the security agencies to be on the look out for perpetrators of such crimes.

a6958.speaker: Togbe Okae Debra, representative of the chiefs of Abutia
a6958.name: Togbe Okae Debra
a6958.title: representative of the chiefs of Abutia
a6958.speech: Pledged the support of the traditional area to partner the project to achieve its purpose.

a6958.speaker: US State Department's 2017 Trafficking in Persons Report
a6958.name: US State Department's 2017 Trafficking in Persons Report
a6958.speech: Ghana is a source, transit, and destination country for men, women, and children subjected to forced labour and sex trafficking.

a7205.speaker: Enoch Godongwana, South African Finance Minister
a7205.name: Enoch Godongwana
a7205.title: South African Finance Minister
a7205.speech: "In the last year alone, our public sector health system lost close to 9 000 health workers." ; "We did not have the money to retain or replace them even after reprioritising funds budgeted for consumables and medicines."

a7205.speaker: Enoch Godongwana, South African Finance Minister
a7205.name: Enoch Godongwana
a7205.title: South African Finance Minister
a7205.speech: Said South Africa's high debt-service costs, which will come to R389.6-million in the 2024/5 financial year, prevent it from spending more on health: "This [debt] translates to 22 cents of every rand we raise in revenue. It is more than what we spend on health, the police and basic education." ; said accruals - unpaid invoices in the public health sector from the previous financial year - also ballooned to nearly R22 billion: "This means that the money allocated to departments ends up paying for previous services and goods rather than for the current needs, setting off a vicious cycle of budget shortfalls, unpaid invoices, and a crisis in cashflow and the planning and predictability of budgets." ; "This is an untenable situation that we could not leave unresolved."

a7205.speaker: South African health ministry (2024 report)
a7205.name: South African health ministry (2024 report)
a7205.speech: Reported that public health sector vacancy rates ranged from 5.48% in the Western Cape up to 22.4% in the Free State.

a7205.speaker: South African health department
a7205.name: South African health department
a7205.speech: Says part of why they can't afford to fill all doctor positions in the state sector is because doctors' salaries are too high - and that cutting the overtime of those already employed would open up budgets to employ others.

a7205.speaker: Percy Mahlathi, South African health department official overseeing hospital services and human resources
a7205.name: Percy Mahlathi
a7205.title: South African health department official overseeing hospital services and human resources
a7205.speech: Told Health Beat in February that doctors in the public health system earn disproportionately higher salaries compared with other professionals: "With the legal profession, many first-year workers would be earning R15 to 20 000 a month. But our health service doctors, with overtime, are earning about R80 to 90 000." ; says redistribution would be a better approach, and that some provinces have already begun restricting overtime to eight hours weekly, potentially saving 50% of current overtime expenditures.

a7205.speaker: Ames Dhai, vice chairperson of the South African Medical Association (SAMA)
a7205.name: Ames Dhai
a7205.title: vice chairperson of the South African Medical Association (SAMA)
a7205.speech: Told Bhekisisa's TV programme, Health Beat, that there's more than enough money to employ all doctors in the country and that the problem lies with the way the health department manages its budget: "Between 2009 and 2013, close to R24 billion was lost due to corruption. So how can the state say it doesn't have enough money?" ; "The problem is the state has fallen behind in its obligation to employ doctors to deliver healthcare to patients in need." ; "It's a huge indictment on the state."

a7205.speaker: Aaron Motsoaledi, South African Health Minister
a7205.name: Aaron Motsoaledi
a7205.title: South African Health Minister
a7205.speech: Told the health portfolio committee in Parliament in February that the health department would need R1.9 billion to employ 1 500 doctors, and that the department had not "anticipated the subsequent economic difficulties, which had severely impacted its ability to absorb new graduates into the workforce".

a7205.speaker: Aaron Motsoaledi, South African Health Minister
a7205.name: Aaron Motsoaledi
a7205.title: South African Health Minister
a7205.speech: According to Motsoaledi, South Africa produces 3 600 doctors per year - up from 1 200 in 2011 - and once doctors have completed their community service year the government simply doesn't have enough money to employ all the doctors the country produces.

a7205.speaker: Theresa Brummer, unemployed post-community service doctor
a7205.name: Theresa Brummer
a7205.title: unemployed post-community service doctor
a7205.speech: "I'm holding out that I'll be able to work in government because that's really where I want to work. But you know, I can't hold out forever."

a7388.speaker: United States government
a7388.name: United States government
a7388.speech: Has issued a fervent appeal for all armed forces in Sudan to cease attacks immediately, amid escalating tensions and the looming threat of violence in El Fasher, North Darfur; expressed profound distress over credible reports detailing the destruction of multiple villages west of El Fasher by the RSF and its affiliates.

a7388.speaker: Matthew Miller, State Department Spokesperson
a7388.name: Matthew Miller
a7388.title: State Department Spokesperson
a7388.speech: "We are alarmed by indications of an imminent offensive by the Rapid Support Forces and its affiliated militias. An offensive against El Fasher city would subject civilians to extreme danger, including the hundreds of thousands of displaced persons who have taken refuge there." ; "We also condemn reported indiscriminate aerial bombardments in the region by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and their continued limitations on life-saving humanitarian aid access." ; In a stark message to the leaders of the SAF, RSF and their associated militias, emphasized the critical choice they face: either escalate violence, exacerbating the suffering of their people and risking the stability of the nation, or opt for peace by halting attacks, facilitating humanitarian assistance, and engaging in earnest negotiations to bring an end to the protracted conflict and empower the people of Sudan.

a7388.speaker: UN Secretary-General's office
a7388.name: UN Secretary-General's office
a7388.speech: "The prospect of an attack on the city is deeply troubling, with devastating consequences for the civilian population, already teetering on the brink of famine."

a7388.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a7388.name: Antonio Guterres
a7388.title: UN Secretary-General
a7388.speech: Reiterated his plea to all parties involved to exercise restraint and refrain from further violence in the El Fasher area.

a7388.speaker: United Nations
a7388.name: United Nations
a7388.speech: Raised alarm over the escalating tensions in El Fasher; reports indicate that the RSF is encircling the city, hinting at a coordinated assault, while the Sudanese Armed Forces position themselves for potential engagement.

a7400.speaker: ‘Mampine Mothae, Principal, Maseru Day High School
a7400.name: ‘Mampine Mothae
a7400.title: Principal, Maseru Day High School
a7400.speech: Said that they are so happy about the initiative YAP has taken in assisting her students: “We are very pleased that you chose to come to our school, you came at the right time since it is the beginning of the year. In helping these people, you are showing them that they are important because children, who are cared for, have vigilant minds.”

a7400.speaker: Tlalane Ntili, Senior YAP Officer
a7400.name: Tlalane Ntili
a7400.title: Senior YAP Officer
a7400.speech: Said they got interested in Maseru Day High School because they were caught by its name and that it is their first time as YAP to host such an event: “The ‘Day' was what actually interested us to come to the school so that eventually we can learn the history of how the name came about.”

a7400.speaker: Lintle Mosala, Public Relations Officer, Maseru City Council (MCC)
a7400.name: Lintle Mosala
a7400.title: Public Relations Officer, Maseru City Council (MCC)
a7400.speech: Said that as MCC they have donated two trash cans to the school in order to inspire cleanliness: “We want to instil cleanliness to the schools so that students can stop littering everywhere. We are on a campaign of keeping the environment clean and there are penalties for littering around”; said that they need everybody to ‘police the environment around them' because a healthy and clean environment is everyone's responsibility.

a7400.speaker: Sechaba Mokoqo, YAP
a7400.name: Sechaba Mokoqo
a7400.title: YAP
a7400.speech: Indicated that the programme is aimed at equipping academically qualified and non-qualified youth with temporary jobs across the country in order to give them work experience: “From 2023 up to today we have had more than 5 000 youths from higher learning institutions who have been given jobs by YAP. We have three categories in this program, for youth from the universities, youth who only went to high school level and youth who did not go to school at all. All these youths are given an opportunity to work and beat unemployment.”

a7400.speaker: Mafata Mafata, Lesotho College of Education
a7400.name: Mafata Mafata
a7400.title: Lesotho College of Education
a7400.speech: Said that the students at Maseru Day High School are very lucky to have been given stationery and sanitary towels: “You are very lucky again because as students you have teachers who always take a very good care of you; school is a home away from home.”

a7432.speaker: The author’s firm (own analysis of 13 African countries)
a7432.name: The author’s firm (own analysis of 13 African countries)
a7432.speech: Estimates an annual financing gap of $108.9 billion to $149.9 billion for those countries collectively to build enough infrastructure to meet the basic United Nations sustainable development goals alone.

a7432.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB) estimates
a7432.name: African Development Bank (AfDB) estimates
a7432.speech: According to AfDB estimates, the continent needs roughly $86.7 billion of external financing per year to meet the objectives of Agenda 2063, of which 76% would have to be devoted to infrastructure, underlining the considerable impact of infrastructure on the continent’s resources.

a7432.speaker: Forthcoming report by the author’s firm
a7432.name: Forthcoming report by the author’s firm
a7432.speech: Analysing the main infrastructure financiers on the continent, finds that African governments themselves contribute around 38% of the continent’s infrastructure financing, making them the main contributors rather than external financiers; African regional banks such as the AfDB, the Development Bank of Southern Africa and the West African Development Bank contribute around 8%.

a7432.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB) research
a7432.name: African Development Bank (AfDB) research
a7432.speech: According to AfDB research, $2.2 billion of infrastructure financing commitments were made by the Arab Coordination Group.

a7432.speaker: US Foreign Assistance data
a7432.name: US Foreign Assistance data
a7432.speech: Data from US Foreign Assistance show that funding levels for African countries for “economic development” fluctuated between $1 and $2 billion over the period 2012-2022; US funding for health and for humanitarian aid in Africa are each three times larger.

a7432.speaker: Paolo Gomes
a7432.name: Paolo Gomes
a7432.speech: As Paolo Gomes explained at an event organised by our firm in 2022, a borrowers’ club that pools risks for creditors could secure them returns several times higher in the medium and long term.

a7432.speaker: The author’s own analysis (Rugare Mukanganga)
a7432.name: The author’s own analysis (Rugare Mukanganga)
a7432.speech: Suggests that most of the Global Infrastructure Hub’s estimates are based on old data and at the bottom of the scale, not necessarily assuming that countries need to meet the SDGs or Agenda 2063.

a7485.speaker: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba, Minister for Finance of Tanzania
a7485.name: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba
a7485.title: Minister for Finance of Tanzania
a7485.speech: Said that the project’s implementation would stimulate growth in the agricultural sector by enhancing farmers’ productivity through access to affordable capital. “This initiative will provide medium and long-term sub-loans to farmers, production groups and agriculture-related enterprises, enabling them to invest in modern farming practices, quality inputs and advanced technologies.” He further noted that the increased financial support would promote crop diversification, the adoption of climate-smart agricultural practices and contribute to food security, rural development and overall economic stability.

a7485.speaker: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba, Minister for Finance of Tanzania
a7485.name: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba
a7485.title: Minister for Finance of Tanzania
a7485.speech: Said the support is aligned with the current National Five-Year Development Plan, which focuses on boosting competitiveness and industrialisation for human development. “This plan aims to increase efficiency and productivity by utilising available resources” ; “It also aligns with the Agricultural Sector Development Plan II, which emphasises strengthening and promoting agricultural mechanisation, ensuring food and nutrition security, improving market access and increasing value addition.”

a7485.speaker: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba, Minister for Finance of Tanzania
a7485.name: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba
a7485.title: Minister for Finance of Tanzania
a7485.speech: Noted that the agreement represents a continuation of growing support, as reflected by the increasing number of bilateral development projects funded by the government of Japan through Official Development Assistance; explained that Tanzania has benefited from Japanese support for over 60 years, particularly in sectors such as agriculture, water, health, energy, transportation and education, with a strong focus on capacity building.

a7485.speaker: Ms Katsura Miyazaki, Executive Senior Vice-President (JICA)
a7485.name: Ms Katsura Miyazaki
a7485.title: Executive Senior Vice-President (JICA)
a7485.speech: Explained that the support aims to improve agricultural productivity and farmers’ incomes by promoting mechanisation within the value chains of key crops. “The main focus of this Two-Step Loan Project is on four priority crops: rice, maize, wheat and sunflower, which are featured in Tanzania’s Five-Year Development Plan, FYDP III. The project will strengthen value chains and contribute to food security.” She added that the project will also support the horticulture sector, creating employment opportunities for women and youths while fostering financial inclusion.

a7485.speaker: Ms Katsura Miyazaki, Executive Senior Vice-President (JICA)
a7485.name: Ms Katsura Miyazaki
a7485.title: Executive Senior Vice-President (JICA)
a7485.speech: Highlighted that through the promotion of agricultural technology, JICA will contribute to Climate-Smart Agriculture, in alignment with the prioritised policies of the Tanzania Agricultural Development Bank (TADB). “JICA has been actively supporting FYDP III and the Agricultural Sector Development Programme Phase II and we will continue to collaborate with Tanzania to align with the Tanzania Development Vision 2025.” She added that JICA is ready to move forward with another key financial initiative for agricultural development, the Tanzania Food Systems Resilience Programme (TFSRP), a co-financing project with the World Bank.

a7485.speaker: Mr Frank Nyabundege, TADB Managing Director
a7485.name: Mr Frank Nyabundege
a7485.title: TADB Managing Director
a7485.speech: Said the five-year project is designed to tackle key challenges by facilitating financial intermediary functions related to agricultural and rural development finance. “Through this partnership, TADB will provide medium and long-term sub-loans to farmer groups, cooperatives, agribusinesses and other beneficiaries nationwide. Our goal is to increase agricultural productivity, enhance value chains, promote rural development, strengthen food security and foster the commercialisation and industrialisation of the agricultural sector.”

a7485.speaker: Mr Frank Nyabundege, TADB Managing Director
a7485.name: Mr Frank Nyabundege
a7485.title: TADB Managing Director
a7485.speech: Highlighted that the loan interest rate is a favourable single-digit rate of 9 per cent, and that maize will be targeted in the regions of Iringa, Njombe, Songwe, Rukwa, Katavi and Ruvuma, rice in Arusha, Kilimanjaro, Manyara and Mbeya, while sunflower will be targeted in the Central Corridor and Southern Highlands ; “By focusing on these specific regions and crops, the project will not only enhance productivity but also contribute to sustainable agricultural practices, improve farmers’ livelihoods and strengthen local economies.”
